questions.question: What is SAP EWM?
questions.answer: SAP Extended Warehouse Management is SAP's advanced warehouse management solution for controlling and optimizing all warehouse processes: goods receipt, putaway, picking, packing, shipping, internal movements, physical inventory, and automation integration. It supports high-volume, complex warehouses with features like wave management, labor management, slotting, and material flow control.

questions.question: How is EWM different from classic SAP WM (LE-WM)?
questions.answer: EWM offers granular process control (storage control, activity areas, work centers), warehouse orders with creation rules, wave management, RF framework, labor management, MFS for automation, yard management, and value-added services - most of which classic WM lacks or supports only rudimentarily. WM is in maintenance mode; SAP's strategic product is EWM, and classic WM support inside S/4HANA is only via compatibility scope (Stock Room Management).

questions.question: What is embedded EWM vs decentralized EWM?
questions.answer: Embedded EWM runs inside the S/4HANA core system, sharing the database, master data, and reducing CIF dependency. Decentralized EWM runs on a separate system (EWM on S/4HANA or SCM server) connected to one or more ERP systems, giving isolation and independent availability at the cost of integration overhead (CIF, qRFC).

questions.question: When would you recommend decentralized EWM over embedded?
questions.answer: When the warehouse must keep running independently of ERP downtime or release cycles, when one EWM serves multiple ERP systems, when warehouse volumes are extremely high and need isolated sizing, or when the warehouse is operated by a 3PL with separate governance.

questions.question: What is Stock Room Management in S/4HANA?
questions.answer: It is the compatibility-scope continuation of classic WM inside S/4HANA with a restricted feature set (no waves, no RF framework enhancements, no new development). It is meant as a bridge for simple warehouses before moving to EWM.

questions.question: Name the main EWM document types in the process flow.
questions.answer: Inbound: notification/expected delivery, inbound delivery, warehouse tasks/orders. Outbound: outbound delivery request, outbound delivery order, warehouse tasks/orders, outbound delivery. Internal: posting changes, stock transfers, ad-hoc warehouse tasks, physical inventory documents.

questions.question: What is the warehouse request concept?
questions.answer: A warehouse request is the EWM-internal representation of a demand to move stock (e.g., an inbound delivery or outbound delivery order). Warehouse tasks are created with reference to a warehouse request, which carries the delivery data into warehouse execution.

questions.question: Which communication technology connects ERP and decentralized EWM?
questions.answer: Primarily qRFC (queued RFC) for deliveries and confirmations, and CIF (Core Interface) for master data such as products, plants, customers, vendors, and classes/characteristics. Some scenarios also use IDocs and web services, but qRFC/CIF is the classic backbone.

questions.question: What replaced CIF in embedded EWM in S/4HANA?
questions.answer: In embedded EWM, most master data (product, business partner, plant) is read directly from the S/4HANA core, so CIF is largely unnecessary; only a few objects still require synchronization. This is one of embedded EWM's biggest simplifications.

questions.question: What is the Post Processing Framework (PPF) used for in EWM?
questions.answer: PPF triggers follow-up actions from documents - printing HU labels and pick lists, sending messages to ERP, creating follow-on documents - based on conditions evaluated at document save. Failed actions can be analyzed and reprocessed in SPPFP.

questions.question: What are the main EWM master data objects?
questions.answer: Warehouse product (global + warehouse-specific views), packaging specifications, storage bins, fixed bin assignments, resources, work centers, routes, business partners, and batches/serial numbers where relevant.

questions.question: What is the warehouse monitor and why is it central to support?
questions.answer: /SCWM/MON is the operational cockpit showing documents, stock, HUs, WOs/WTs, queues, waves, exceptions, and alerts with drill-down and follow-on actions (confirm, cancel, unblock). In support, nearly every incident starts with monitor analysis.

questions.question: What is the difference between an outbound delivery request (ODR) and outbound delivery order (ODO)?
questions.answer: The ODR is the inbound message copy of the ERP delivery - largely display-only. The ODO is the active EWM working document created from the ODR where picking, packing, staging, and GI are executed. After GI, the final outbound delivery (FD) represents the completed shipment.

questions.question: Which processes can EWM control that go beyond moving pallets?
questions.answer: Value-added services (labelling, kitting), quality inspection integration, yard and dock management, labor management with engineered standards, slotting/rearrangement, cross-docking, production supply, and material flow control of automated equipment.

questions.question: What is a warehouse door and staging area in EWM?
questions.answer: Doors are the physical dock positions where trucks load/unload, modeled as master data linked to staging areas - interim zones where goods wait between door and final process. Determination rules assign deliveries to staging areas and doors automatically.

questions.question: What is the availability group concept?
questions.answer: Availability groups map EWM stock to ERP storage locations. Combined with stock type, they determine in which ERP storage location EWM stock is reflected - e.g., ROD (received on dock) vs AFS (available for sale) - enabling location-accurate ATP in ERP while EWM manages the bins.

questions.question: How does EWM report stock to ERP?
questions.answer: EWM manages bin-level stock itself and communicates only aggregate changes (goods movements, posting changes) to ERP, which keeps storage-location-level stock. ERP never sees bins; EWM never owns valuation.

questions.question: What are queues in EWM (two meanings)?
questions.answer: First, RF/resource queues: logical groupings of warehouse work used to assign tasks to resources. Second, qRFC queues: technical inbound/outbound message queues between ERP and EWM. Interview answers should distinguish both.

questions.question: What is a warehouse process type?
questions.answer: A control object assigned to every warehouse task that bundles process behavior: document category, activity, storage process references, confirmation requirements, stock type handling, and determination influence for putaway/removal. It is determined per delivery item via determination rules.

questions.question: What is the difference between warehouse task and warehouse order?
questions.answer: A warehouse task (WT) is the elementary move instruction (product or HU, source, destination, quantity). A warehouse order (WO) is the executable work package grouping one or more WTs for a resource, built by warehouse order creation rules (WOCR).

questions.question: What does 'delivery-based' vs 'stock-based' mean for EWM documents?
questions.answer: Delivery-based processes reference a warehouse request from a delivery (inbound/outbound flows). Stock-based (ad-hoc) movements act directly on stock without a delivery, e.g., internal replenishment or manual bin-to-bin transfers.

questions.question: What is the role of the storage control concept?
questions.answer: Storage control orchestrates multi-step movements: process-oriented (POSC) defines process steps (e.g., unload > deconsolidate > putaway), layout-oriented (LOSC) forces routing via intermediate physical points (e.g., conveyor pick-up/drop-off). Both can combine.

questions.question: Which UI technologies does EWM offer for execution?
questions.answer: SAP GUI transactions, the RF framework (ITSmobile/SAP GUI for HTML on mobile devices), Fiori apps in S/4HANA embedded EWM, and desktop work center transactions for packing, deconsolidation, and PI.

questions.question: What is a work center in EWM?
questions.answer: A physical location with a specialized UI where goods are processed rather than just moved - packing, deconsolidation, VAS, quality inspection, counting. It is linked to a storage bin and configured with layouts defining allowed actions.

questions.question: What are the deployment options for EWM today?
questions.answer: Embedded EWM in S/4HANA (basic and advanced licensing), decentralized EWM on S/4HANA, and legacy EWM 9.x on SCM Server (nearing the end of mainstream maintenance on the Business Suite 7 timeline - migration planning is expected in interviews). Cloud: EWM capabilities within S/4HANA Cloud editions.

questions.question: What is basic vs advanced EWM licensing in S/4HANA?
questions.answer: Basic (included in S/4HANA) covers core receiving, putaway, picking, shipping, PI, and simple processes. Advanced (licensed) adds MFS, labor management, slotting, yard management, wave management, kitting/VAS, cartonization, and dock appointment scheduling, among others.

questions.question: How do alerts work in EWM?
questions.answer: The alert monitor surfaces exceptional situations (overdue deliveries, stuck queues, capacity overflows) based on configured alert types; alerts can trigger follow-up like emails or workflow. Support teams use them for proactive monitoring.

questions.question: What is the Easy Graphics Framework (EGF)?
questions.answer: A cockpit framework for graphical KPI tiles over warehouse data (workload, throughput, resource utilization) - the classic EWM graphical dashboard; in S/4HANA, Fiori overview pages increasingly take this role.

questions.question: What is a 3PL scenario in EWM terms?
questions.answer: The warehouse operator manages stock it does not own. EWM supports this via separate party entitled to dispose, multiple availability groups/owners on the same bins, and billing-relevant service documentation (with EWM billing or integration to SD).

questions.question: Sketch the end-to-end outbound message flow between ERP and decentralized EWM.
questions.answer: ERP creates the outbound delivery > qRFC sends it to EWM > EWM builds ODR/ODO > warehouse executes picking/packing/staging > EWM posts GI > qRFC sends the GI and changes back > ERP updates the delivery, stock, and triggers billing. Any break in the qRFC chain is a classic support case.

questions.question: What is a warehouse number in EWM and how does it relate to ERP?
questions.answer: The warehouse number is the top organizational unit representing one physical warehouse complex. The ERP warehouse number is mapped to the EWM warehouse number; ERP plant/storage location combinations are assigned to it so deliveries route to the right warehouse.

questions.question: What is a storage type? Give examples.
questions.answer: A physical or logical area of the warehouse with uniform properties and rules - e.g., high rack, narrow aisle, bulk floor, pick face, GR zone, GI zone, clarification zone, doors, yard. Behavior like HU requirement, capacity checks, and strategies are controlled at storage type level.

questions.question: What are storage type roles?
questions.answer: Each storage type has a role: standard storage, identification point, pick point, staging area group, work center, doors, yard, or clarification. The role determines which processes may use it and how the system treats stock there.

questions.question: What is a storage section and when do you use it?
questions.answer: A subdivision of a storage type grouping bins with similar characteristics (e.g., fast-mover section near the aisle start, heavy-goods section at floor level). Putaway can filter or prioritize by section via the storage section search sequence.

questions.question: What is a storage bin and what key attributes does it carry?
questions.answer: The addressable stock location within a storage type: coordinates, bin type (size), maximum weight/volume, section, activity area assignment, verification field for RF, fixed-bin flags, and blocks. Bins are master data, mass-creatable via templates.

questions.question: What is a bin type and how is it used?
questions.answer: Bin type classifies bin dimensions/capacity classes (e.g., half-pallet slot, full-pallet slot, shelf). Putaway rules can match HU types to allowed bin types, ensuring physical fit.

questions.question: What is an activity area?
questions.answer: A grouping of bins for a specific activity (picking, putaway, PI, replenishment) with a defined sort sequence. Activity areas decouple execution sequencing from physical storage structure - the same bins can belong to different activity areas per activity with different sort orders.

questions.question: Why is bin sorting in activity areas important?
questions.answer: The sort sequence drives the travel path of warehouse order items (pick path optimization). Wrong or missing sorting produces zigzag picking and destroys productivity; re-sorting is done via activity area bin sorting generation.

questions.question: What is the difference between storage type search sequence for putaway and activity areas?
questions.answer: The storage type search sequence determines WHERE stock should go or come from (strategy scope); activity areas determine in WHAT ORDER work is executed within the selected bins. One targets determination, the other execution sequencing.

questions.question: What is a work center's organizational placement?
questions.answer: A work center is tied to a storage type with an appropriate role and references a specific bin (or bins) where the processing happens; its layout configuration defines tabs/actions like packing, deconsolidation, counting, or VAS.

questions.question: How are doors modeled and determined?
questions.answer: Doors are org units assigned to the warehouse with links to staging areas; determination uses staging area and door determination groups from the delivery (route, carrier, warehouse process) to find the right staging area/door combination.

questions.question: What is a yard in EWM?
questions.answer: The yard models the area outside the building - checkpoints, parking spaces, and doors as yard bins - so trucks/transportation units can be checked in, moved, and tracked like stock with yard movements.

questions.question: What is the supply chain unit (SCU) concept?
questions.answer: SCUs are location master records (from the SCM foundation) representing the warehouse, shipping offices, or partners in EWM; the warehouse number is linked to an SCU with address and calendar data used in routing and printing.

questions.question: What is a party entitled to dispose?
questions.answer: The business partner that owns the right to control the stock (usually mapped from ERP plant). It separates stock of different owners in the same warehouse - essential for 3PL and multi-plant warehouses.

questions.question: Can one EWM warehouse number serve multiple ERP plants?
questions.answer: Yes - multiple plant/storage location combinations can map to one EWM warehouse; stock is separated by party entitled to dispose/owner, and processes must be designed to respect that separation.

questions.question: What is a storage group/bin access type used for?
questions.answer: Bin access types and storage groups support MFS and resource routing decisions - e.g., which equipment can reach which bins (crane vs forklift zones), preventing tasks assigned to resources that physically cannot execute them.

questions.question: How do you mass-create storage bins?
questions.answer: Define bin structure templates with coordinate patterns, then generate bins via /SCWM/LS10 (structure-based generation) or upload them from file via /SCWM/SBUP, followed by activity area assignment and bin sorting. Single bins are created in /SCWM/LS01; migration tools handle cutover loads.

questions.question: What is the clarification zone for?
questions.answer: A dedicated storage type where problem stock is routed - unreadable labels, overages, damaged goods - so exceptions leave the main flow and are resolved by specialists without blocking dock or line operations.

questions.question: What is an identification point (I-point)?
questions.answer: A storage type role where inbound goods are identified/verified before final putaway in layout-oriented storage control - typical in automated high-bay entries where pallets are checked (contour, weight, label) at a fixed point.

questions.question: What is a pick point?
questions.answer: The counterpart for outbound in LOSC: goods from an automated area are brought to a pick point where partial quantities are removed, and the remainder returns to storage. Common with unit-load ASRS serving case picking.

questions.question: How do you decide storage type granularity in a design?
questions.answer: Split by physically or procedurally different behavior: different equipment, capacity logic, strategy, HU rules, or stock segregation needs. Avoid over-fragmentation - every storage type multiplies configuration (strategies, sequences, POSC steps).

questions.question: What controls whether a storage type requires HUs?
questions.answer: The HU requirement setting on the storage type: full HU management (all stock in HUs), without HUs, or mixed. GR/GI zones typically require HUs; some pick faces run without HUs for loose-piece handling.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of bins per warehouse - practical concerns?
questions.answer: There is no meaningful hard limit for typical projects; the practical concerns are monitor/report performance, PI scope, and activity area sorting maintenance. Good naming conventions and archiving discipline matter more than the count.

questions.question: What naming convention would you recommend for bins?
questions.answer: Encode aisle-stack-level (e.g., A01-05-03) consistently with fixed-width segments so sorting, RF verification, and label printing are predictable; keep check digits/verification values distinct from the visible coordinate.

questions.question: What is a verification field on a bin?
questions.answer: The value the RF user must scan/type to prove physical presence at the bin (often the bin coordinate or a check digit). It guards against confirming moves at the wrong location.

questions.question: How do blocks work at bin and storage type level?
questions.answer: Bins can be blocked for putaway, removal, or both (with reason codes) individually or en masse; storage types can also be excluded via strategy filters. Blocks are respected by determination but can be overridden by ad-hoc moves with authorization.

questions.question: How is the warehouse structure transported vs maintained as master data?
questions.answer: Storage types, sections, activity area definitions, roles, and sequences are customizing (transported); bins, fixed bin assignments, and sorting are master data maintained directly in each system (or migrated). Confusing the two causes go-live gaps.

questions.question: What is an activity in EWM org terms?
questions.answer: Activities (e.g., putaway PTWY, picking PICK, counting) classify work within processes; combined with activity areas they drive queue determination and bin sorting - the bridge between org structure and execution assignment.

questions.question: What is the role of the warehouse number-level settings ('warehouse number control')?
questions.answer: Global defaults per warehouse: weight/volume units, time zone, delivery-relevant settings, HU number ranges, default process behavior. Many subtle behaviors trace back here, so support consultants must know this customizing node.

questions.question: A new mezzanine with 2,000 bins is being added. Outline your org-structure work.
questions.answer: Create/extend storage type(s) with correct role and HU settings, define sections and bin types, generate bins via templates, assign and sort activity areas, extend putaway/removal search sequences and WOCRs, extend queues and printer determination, update replenishment and PI scopes, then test determination end-to-end before releasing to operations.

questions.question: What is the warehouse product master?
questions.answer: The product master extended with warehouse-number-specific views (/SCWM/MAT1): putaway/removal control indicators, storage type/section indicators, fixed bin relevance, replenishment min/max, PI settings, and slotting parameters. It steers nearly every determination for that SKU in that warehouse.

questions.question: Which product fields drive putaway determination?
questions.answer: Putaway control indicator, storage section indicator, bin type preferences, HU type dependencies, capacity data (weight/volume/dimensions), and slotting-derived condition values. They feed the storage type search sequence and capacity checks.

questions.question: Which product fields drive stock removal?
questions.answer: Stock removal control indicator (mapping to the removal search sequence), stock determination and valuation-relevant settings, and quantity classifications that select full-pallet vs case vs piece logic per requested quantity.

questions.question: What is a packaging specification (packspec)?
questions.answer: Master data describing how a product is packed level by level (e.g., 24 EA per carton, 40 cartons per pallet) including HU types, dimensions, weights, and work steps. It powers palletization at GR, cartonization proposals, replenishment quantities, and rounding.

questions.question: How are packspecs determined at runtime?
questions.answer: Via the condition technique: determination procedures with condition tables (e.g., by product, product/customer) find the valid packspec for a process like putaway palletization or pick-HU proposal. Missing condition records are a classic 'why is no packspec found' ticket.

questions.question: What is the difference between packspec and HU type?
questions.answer: The HU type classifies a handling unit's physical category (Euro pallet, industrial pallet, tote); the packspec describes the full packing structure and quantities. Packspec levels reference HU types.

questions.question: What are fixed storage bins and when are they used?
questions.answer: Bins permanently assigned to a product, typically pick faces in piece/case-pick areas. Putaway/removal can prefer fixed bins, and replenishment refills them based on min/max quantities from the product master or bin assignment.

questions.question: How do you maintain fixed bin assignments at scale?
questions.answer: /SCWM/BINMAT for assignments, with slotting proposing optimal fixed bins and rearrangement moving stock when assignments change; mass maintenance/upload tools for projects.

questions.question: What is slotting in EWM?
questions.answer: An optimization function that calculates ideal storage parameters per product - storage type/section, bin type, fixed bin - from demand, dimensions, and weight data. Results can be simulated, released to the product master, and executed physically via rearrangement.

questions.question: What is rearrangement?
questions.answer: The execution counterpart of slotting: it creates warehouse tasks to move stock so physical placement matches the (new) optimal slotting, e.g., promoting a product to a better pick face.

questions.question: What master data does a resource have?
questions.answer: A resource represents a user/equipment combination: resource type and group, queues via the group, allowed bin access types, position management settings, and current queue/task assignment. Users are linked to resources for RF work.

questions.question: What is a resource type vs resource group?
questions.answer: Resource type describes capability (forklift, picker-with-cart, crane) including HU type compatibility and vertical movement; resource group bundles resources for queue sequence assignment - the work-routing dimension.

questions.question: How does queue determination work?
questions.answer: Queues are determined for warehouse tasks from criteria like activity area, activity, source/destination, and process type via the queue determination table. Resources receive work from queues listed in their group's queue sequence.

questions.question: What are the batch management touchpoints in EWM master data?
questions.answer: The product must be batch-managed consistently with ERP; batch master records replicate (CIF class/characteristics in decentralized setups). EWM supports batch-specific stock, documentary batches, and characteristics-based determination (e.g., FEFO via shelf-life).

questions.question: How does shelf-life/FEFO work in EWM?
questions.answer: With SLED data on batches, stock removal sorts eligible quantities by expiry (FEFO) when the removal rule uses shelf-life sorting; goods receipt can enforce minimum remaining shelf life checks.

questions.question: What are quantity classifications?
questions.answer: Classifications like full pallet, case, piece derived from packspec levels; they let determinations differentiate: full-pallet quantities from reserve, cases from case-pick, pieces from piece-pick - both for putaway and removal.

questions.question: What is a stock determination group used for?
questions.answer: It controls preference logic when multiple stock categories could satisfy demand (e.g., use up consignment before own stock). Configured stock determination rules are assigned via the product.

questions.question: What is the 'process block' on product level?
questions.answer: Products can be blocked warehouse-specifically for putaway/removal/processes (status management), stopping new tasks while allowing corrections - used during recalls, quality holds, or data fixes.

questions.question: How do serial number profiles work in EWM?
questions.answer: Serial requirement levels per warehouse: no serials, serials at document items, or serials in warehouse (bin-level tracking). The profile decides where scans are mandatory (GR, WT confirmation, GI) - deeper tracking means more scans and more support cases.

questions.question: What is an alternative unit of measure issue that hits EWM often?
questions.answer: Deliveries or packspecs referencing a UoM (e.g., PAL, CAR) that lacks a conversion in the product master cause qRFC failures or determination errors; UoM governance is core master data hygiene.

questions.question: What product data does slotting need to be meaningful?
questions.answer: Accurate dimensions and weights, demand history/forecast, packspec quantities, and correct storage requirement inputs. Garbage in, garbage out - slotting on bad cube data produces unusable bin assignments.

questions.question: What is the difference between warehouse product and global product data?
questions.answer: Global data (identifiers, base UoM, batch flag, serialization) is shared; warehouse-specific views hold per-warehouse process control. Support must check both layers when determinations misbehave.

questions.question: How do work center layouts relate to master data?
questions.answer: The layout is customizing, but each concrete work center is master data tied to bins/storage type; packing stations additionally use packspecs and printer determination records - three layers that must align.

questions.question: What are common root causes when 'no packspec found' occurs?
questions.answer: Missing/invalid condition record, wrong determination procedure assigned to the process, packspec not released/active, product data (e.g., UoM) mismatching the packspec level, or access sequence field values differing (customer-specific packspec expected).

questions.question: How is master data migrated at go-live?
questions.answer: Bins and sorting via templates/migration cockpit or LSMW-style loads, product warehouse views via mass maintenance/BAPIs, packspecs via upload programs, fixed bins via /SCWM/BINMAT uploads, initial stock via PI-style stock upload with HUs. Each load needs count-based validation evidence.

questions.question: What is a documentary batch?
questions.answer: A lightweight batch reference used when full batch management is off but batch documentation is legally needed (tracking which batch went to which customer) - EWM records it without batch-based stock separation.

questions.question: Why can duplicate EAN/GTIN entries hurt RF processes?
questions.answer: RF identification often scans EAN to find the product; duplicates make identification ambiguous, causing wrong-product risks or scan rejections. EAN uniqueness checks belong in the master data quality program.

questions.question: What is the role of business partners in EWM master data?
questions.answer: Customers, vendors, carriers, and organizational parties are BPs; routes, staging determination, and printing use BP data. In decentralized setups, BP replication issues surface as delivery interface errors.

questions.question: How do min/max replenishment parameters get set well?
questions.answer: From demand analysis: max approx. a few days of forecast demand bounded by bin capacity; min set to cover replenishment lead time plus safety. Slotting can propose them; periodic review keeps them aligned to seasonality.

questions.question: A product picks slowly and denials are frequent; which master data would you audit first?
questions.answer: Fixed bin assignment and its min/max vs actual demand, packspec correctness (rounding and pick UoM), removal control indicator and search sequence fit, quantity classification thresholds, weight/volume accuracy, and whether slotting placement matches the current demand class.

questions.question: What does CIF transfer to a decentralized EWM?
questions.answer: Master data: products, plants, storage locations (as SCUs), customers, vendors, shipping points, and classes/characteristics for batches. Integration models are generated (CFM1) and activated (CFM2) per object type.

questions.question: What is an integration model?
questions.answer: A named selection of master data objects to transfer via CIF. Activation compares the new model against active ones and sends deltas; models are regenerated on schedule to catch new/changed objects.

questions.question: What are typical CIF failure patterns in support?
questions.answer: Queue entries failing on missing prerequisites (class not in target, UoM conversion missing), inactive/obsolete integration models missing new materials, filter gaps (plant not included), and sequence problems when dependent objects transfer out of order.

questions.question: How do deliveries technically travel between ERP and EWM?
questions.answer: As qRFC messages: ERP outbound queue (SMQ1) to EWM inbound queue (SMQ2) for distribution, and reverse for confirmations/GI. Queue names encode object type and document number (e.g., DLWS + delivery number for outbound delivery distribution), so support can filter SMQ1/SMQ2 quickly and read one document's whole message history in its queue.

questions.question: Why does qRFC process strictly in sequence and why does it matter?
questions.answer: Queues serialize dependent messages per object to preserve consistency (a GI must not overtake its delivery): one failed LUW blocks everything behind it in that same queue. Blast radius depends on queue granularity - delivery queues are document-specific, so one bad delivery blocks only its own follow-ons, while serialized master-data/CIF queues can hold many objects hostage behind a single failure.

questions.question: What is the difference between SMQ1 and SMQ2?
questions.answer: SMQ1 shows outbound queues (messages waiting to leave the sending system); SMQ2 shows inbound queues (messages waiting to be processed by the receiving system). Both sides must be checked for a stuck interface.

questions.question: A queue shows SYSFAIL - your standard operating procedure?
questions.answer: Open the LUW to read the error, reproduce/understand the functional cause, fix the root cause (master data, config, code), then Activate the queue to reprocess. Never delete without documenting the payload; deletion causes silent stock/document divergence.

questions.question: What is /SCWM/ERP_STOCKCHECK and when do you run it?
questions.answer: The stock comparison report between EWM and ERP at product/sloc level. Run scheduled (weekly) and after incidents involving lost messages, queue deletions, or downtime windows; differences are then corrected by controlled postings.

questions.question: How are goods movements reported from EWM to ERP?
questions.answer: GR/GI and posting changes are sent as goods movement messages via qRFC and post in ERP as material documents against the mapped storage locations. Failures leave EWM 'done' but ERP not updated - a top severity pattern.

questions.question: What is delivery split and quantity difference messaging between the systems?
questions.answer: EWM can report picked-quantity differences and splits back to ERP, adjusting delivery quantities before/at GI depending on process settings, keeping billing accurate for short picks.

questions.question: What happens if someone changes an ERP delivery after distribution to EWM?
questions.answer: Changes must flow as delivery update messages; conflicting states (EWM already picking) can reject updates or set blocks requiring clarification. Certain changes are locked once warehouse activity starts - a frequent business complaint to understand.

questions.question: What tools exist to monitor the interface health end-to-end?
questions.answer: SMQ1/SMQ2 (with alerting), qRFC monitor jobs, SLG1 application logs, /SCWM/PRDI-PRDO document flow status, interface-specific monitors like /SCWM/ERP_STOCKCHECK, and CCMS/Solution Manager or Focused Run alerting on queue aging.

questions.question: What is the 'delivery interface' clarification concept?
questions.answer: Messages that cannot post (e.g., unknown product, locked document) can be parked for clarification and reprocessed after correction instead of blocking queues - reducing SYSFAIL chains.

questions.question: Embedded EWM: what integration still exists with S/4 core?
questions.answer: Even embedded, delivery documents synchronize between LE and EWM layers, goods movements post through defined interfaces, and some scenarios queue internally; the difference is no cross-system RFC layer, so fewer failure modes, not zero.

questions.question: What are the classic root causes for a delivery not arriving in EWM?
questions.answer: Stuck/failed queue, delivery incompletion or missing warehouse-relevant data (no warehouse number determined), distribution not triggered (wrong shipping point/sloc mapping), user locks, or EWM-side clarification cases parked unnoticed.

questions.question: What is the difference between an expected goods receipt and an inbound delivery?
questions.answer: The inbound delivery is the confirmed advanced shipping notification basis for GR; expected goods receipt documents (from POs/production orders) let EWM create deliveries warehouse-side when no ASN exists. EGR is pull, ASN is push.

questions.question: Why should support know number range buffering for documents?
questions.answer: Buffered number ranges can produce non-sequential document numbers, confusing business audits; and exhausted/misconfigured ranges stop document creation cold - a rare but severe incident.

questions.question: What is the role of RFC destinations and logical systems in the setup?
questions.answer: Each side addresses the other via logical system + RFC destination with dedicated interface users; authorization or password issues on these users silently fail entire interfaces - check SM59 connection and authorization tests early.

questions.question: Batch replication fails for one product but works for others - suspicion?
questions.answer: That product's batch class/characteristics differ (new characteristic not in target), the batch has values violating target checks, or the CIF model does not include its class - compare with a working product to isolate.

questions.question: How do you handle a planned ERP downtime cleanly for a decentral EWM?
questions.answer: Warehouse can keep working: queues buffer messages. Before: verify queue health, inform sizing of expected backlog. During: monitor queue growth. After: controlled queue activation, watch for SYSFAILs, then run stock reconciliation. Chaos comes from unmonitored retry expiry - covered in the runbook.

questions.question: What is a 'lost update' risk between the systems and its guard-rails?
questions.answer: Parallel changes to the same delivery from both sides can conflict; guards are process discipline (change ownership rules), locks, and update-conflict handling with clarification. Support explains rather than fights these locks.

questions.question: Which master data must exist in EWM before a delivery can process?
questions.answer: Product with warehouse view, packspec if determinations need it, business partners (vendor/customer/carrier), batch (or auto-create via replication), and routes/staging determinants where used. Missing pieces surface as determination or interface errors.

questions.question: What are queue prefixes worth memorizing for EWM support?
questions.answer: Outbound delivery distribution ERP>EWM (DLWS + document number), inbound deliveries (DLWI*), goods movement and confirmation messages EWM>ERP (WM* family), CIF master data (CF*). Exact names vary by release and configuration - the durable skill is filtering SMQ1/SMQ2 by prefix and reading a document's queue as its message timeline.

questions.question: How does serialization of messages per delivery help troubleshooting?
questions.answer: All messages of one delivery share a queue name, so its complete story sits in one place; when analyzing, you read the queue like a timeline of what has and has not arrived.

questions.question: What is an inbound queue 'WAITING' vs 'RUNNING' vs 'SYSFAIL'?
questions.answer: WAITING: behind another queue entry or scheduler backlog. RUNNING: currently processing (stuck RUNNING may be a hanging work process). SYSFAIL: processing failed with an error - open it and read. Different statuses, different playbooks.

questions.question: When would you regenerate vs simply reactivate an integration model?
questions.answer: Reactivate to re-push the same object selection; regenerate (CFM1) when the object set changed (new materials/plants) before activation. Scheduled regenerate+activate jobs are the standard pattern.

questions.question: ERP shows the delivery distributed, EWM has nothing, queues are clean - now what?
questions.answer: Check EWM clarification/parked messages, SLG1 logs around the timestamp, whether the message posted but the document search filters mislead (wrong warehouse/document type), or a middleware/routing misdirect (wrong logical system) - verify in the payload where it actually went.

questions.question: Why is time synchronization between systems relevant?
questions.answer: Timestamps drive latest-change conflict logic, monitoring windows, and debugging correlation; clock skew produces confusing sequences (confirmation apparently before creation) that derail analysis.

questions.question: What belongs in a permanent interface monitoring concept for EWM?
questions.answer: Queue age/failure alerting both directions, daily automated stock comparison, PPF failure sweeps, clarification-case review, interface user credential/authorization change control, and a documented reprocessing SOP with escalation paths - reviewed quarterly.

questions.question: Name three golden rules for qRFC handling in production.
questions.answer: Never delete failed LUWs without recording payload and approval; always fix root cause before activation so the queue does not re-fail; and always check BOTH systems' queues plus the application log before declaring an interface healthy.

title: Inbound Process: GR, Expected Receipts, TUs

questions.question: Walk through the standard EWM inbound flow.
questions.answer: ERP PO/ASN > inbound delivery distributed to EWM > (optional TU check-in and door assignment) > unloading > goods receipt posting > putaway WT creation per storage control > deconsolidation if needed > final putaway confirmation. Stock becomes ERP-visible per availability group mapping at GR.

questions.question: What is a transportation unit (TU) in inbound?
questions.answer: The truck/trailer representation carrying deliveries; TUs support check-in at the gate, door assignment, unloading scope, and yard moves - connecting yard logistics with delivery processing.

questions.question: When does stock become visible in ERP during inbound?
questions.answer: At goods receipt posting in EWM: the GR message posts in ERP into the storage location mapped from the stock type/availability group (often a 'received on dock' sloc first, then AFS after putaway posting change, depending on design).

questions.question: What is the two-step availability design ROD/AFS?
questions.answer: GR posts into ROD (received on dock, availability group 1); final putaway triggers a posting change to AFS (available for sale, group 2). ATP then only sees stock actually stored away - protecting order promising from dock inventory.

questions.question: How does palletization at GR work?
questions.answer: Packspec determination proposes how the delivery quantity splits into HUs (e.g., 40 cases per pallet); the system pre-creates planned HUs/warehouse tasks accordingly - manual repacking remains possible for deviations.

questions.question: What is deconsolidation?
questions.answer: Splitting mixed inbound HUs at a deconsolidation work center into putaway-HUs per destination area, when the putaway WTs of the HU's items target different activity areas beyond a configured limit.

questions.question: What triggers a deconsolidation step in POSC?
questions.answer: Storage process step configuration plus the deconsolidation-relevance logic (mixed HU whose items' destinations differ by activity area/consolidation group); if relevant, the HU first routes to the decon work center.

questions.question: What are typical GR reversal scenarios and their handling?
questions.answer: Wrong delivery/quantity posted: bring stock back to GR-relevant state (cancel/repost putaway WTs), reverse GR (syncs to ERP), correct the delivery, re-post. Discipline matters: reversal after downstream movements requires stock retrieval first.

questions.question: What is an expected goods receipt used for practically?
questions.answer: Warehouses receiving without ASNs generate inbound deliveries in EWM from PO data (EGR documents), enabling receiving to start from the truck arrival rather than waiting for ERP paperwork.

questions.question: What quality options exist at receiving?
questions.answer: QM integration can create inspection lots (via inspection rules) for GR-relevant stock: sampling to a QI work center, full quantity to Q-stock, or skip-lot logic; usage decision then releases stock via posting change.

questions.question: What are usual root causes of 'no putaway bin found' tickets?
questions.answer: Full/blocked bins in target types, capacity check rejections (weight/volume/height/bin type), missing product putaway indicators, search sequence gaps for the product's parameters, HU type vs bin type mismatch, or all candidate types excluded by earlier steps.

questions.question: What is a putaway clarification (posting to clarification zone)?
questions.answer: When determination fails or goods are problematic, stock routes to a clarification storage type where specialists resolve data or physical issues, keeping docks flowing.

questions.question: How do catch weight or batch capture requirements affect GR?
questions.answer: Additional capture steps at GR (batch entry with characteristics, actual weights) become mandatory fields in the GR/RF flows; missing values block posting - design decides where capture is fastest and most accurate.

questions.question: What is the unloading step and when is it explicitly modeled?
questions.answer: As a POSC step with WTs from door to GR-zone bins, used when you need labor tracking, HU-level control, or staging discipline at the dock; simple warehouses often skip explicit unloading.

questions.question: How do returns differ from standard receipts?
questions.answer: Returns arrive unpredictable in quality and packaging: flows typically route via inspection work centers, use separate process types/stock types (blocked/quality), dedicated storage types, and generate disposition decisions (restock, refurbish, scrap).

questions.question: What is the role of the inbound delivery notification (IDN)?
questions.answer: The technical message copy from ERP that becomes/updates the inbound delivery (ID) in EWM - parallel to the ODR/ODO concept outbound; correction handling references the notification layer.

questions.question: How would you receive serialized products efficiently?
questions.answer: Depending on profile: capture serials at GR (scan each) or defer to putaway confirmation; use RF scanning with validation against expected serial lists when ASN carries serials - balancing compliance with dock speed.

questions.question: A GR posts in EWM but ERP shows nothing - top suspects?
questions.answer: Failed/blocked outbound queue EWM>ERP, posting error in ERP (period locked, movement blocked) leaving the message in error state, or availability group/sloc mapping missing so ERP rejects. Check SMQ1 (EWM), the ERP-side logs, and mapping config.

questions.question: How does GR handle over-delivery/under-delivery?
questions.answer: Tolerances from the PO/delivery control whether excess is accepted, rejected, or needs approval; under-delivery leaves the delivery partially received with follow-up (further GR or closing). Warehouses need clear SOPs so clerks do not force wrong quantities.

questions.question: What is a door appointment vs simple check-in?
questions.answer: Dock appointment scheduling plans time slots for carriers in advance (separate component); simple check-in just registers arrival and assigns a door ad hoc. High-volume DCs use appointments to level dock workload.

questions.question: Which monitors do you watch for inbound health?
questions.answer: Warehouse monitor nodes for inbound deliveries (status overview, overdue GRs), open putaway WTs aging, deconsolidation backlog, clarification zone stock, and queue monitors - plus dock KPIs like truck dwell time via TU data.

questions.question: What is 'GR from production' in EWM?
questions.answer: Receipt of finished goods from manufacturing: via inbound deliveries from production orders or direct staging/receipt integration in embedded scenarios, with putaway from a production handover zone - same putaway machinery, different trigger.

questions.question: Why might putaway WTs be created before physical GR and what is the risk?
questions.answer: Some designs create planned WTs from the delivery pre-GR for speed (labels ready at arrival); risk is divergence when actual receipt differs (quantities/damage), requiring task adjustment discipline.

questions.question: What is a handover between POSC steps physically?
questions.answer: Intermediate bins/zones defined per step (e.g., GR zone bin after unloading, decon inbound buffer); each step's WT confirms into the next step's source, keeping system state aligned with physical staging lanes.

questions.question: How do you test inbound configuration changes safely?
questions.answer: In QA with copied master data: run determination simulations, post a scripted receipt set covering single-SKU, mixed HU, QM-relevant, batch, and serialized cases; verify ERP postings and document flows before transport.

questions.question: What is the impact of wrong weight/volume master data at GR?
questions.answer: Wrong palletization proposals (too many/few HUs), capacity check failures or overloads, wrong resource/equipment selection, and distorted labor standards - GR is where bad cube data first hurts.

questions.question: How are damaged goods handled at the dock?
questions.answer: Record with exception codes into damaged/blocked stock type, route to clarification/quality area, document (photos, notes) for vendor claims, and keep them out of standard putaway - all within the receiving flow, not after.

questions.question: What is the role of process types in inbound?
questions.answer: The warehouse process type per delivery item controls GR behavior, storage process selection, stock type defaults, and putaway WT parameters; determination rules assign it from delivery data - misdetermination is a frequent root cause.

questions.question: Inbound KPIs a support/ops review should track?
questions.answer: Dock-to-stock time, GR postings per hour, putaway WT aging, deconsolidation throughput, clarification-zone dwell, putaway accuracy (bin denials during later picks), and queue/interface error rates for inbound objects.

questions.question: Truck at door, system down for 30 minutes - what is your business continuity guidance?
questions.answer: Follow the documented degraded-mode SOP: continue physical unloading into marked staging lanes with paper/mobile-offline capture of HU labels and quantities, hold GR postings, then post catch-up in sequence after recovery with a verification count - never invent postings from memory.

questions.question: What determines the putaway storage type sequence?
questions.answer: The putaway control indicator from the warehouse product (possibly slotting-derived) plus process type/HU data feed the storage type search sequence in customizing; the sequence lists candidate storage types in priority order.

questions.question: Name standard putaway strategies (bin determination rules) in EWM.
questions.answer: Manual entry, fixed bin, general storage (any suitable bin), addition to existing stock, empty bin, near fixed picking bin, pallet storage (bin-type based), and bulk storage - configured per storage type.

questions.question: How does 'addition to existing stock' work and its constraints?
questions.answer: The system searches bins already holding the same product/batch with capacity left, respecting mixed-storage rules; it consolidates stock to save space but can concentrate risk and complicate FIFO if used carelessly.

questions.question: What is the 'empty bin' strategy with sorting?
questions.answer: Selects the next empty bin per the storage type's bin sorting (cross-line stock placement sequence), spreading products for access efficiency; sorting generation defines the fill pattern across aisles.

questions.question: Explain 'near fixed picking bin' putaway.
questions.answer: Reserve quantities are placed close to the product's fixed pick bin (same aisle/area) to shorten later replenishment travel - powerful in case-pick operations with reserve overhead.

questions.question: What is bulk storage in EWM?
questions.answer: Block/floor storage where quantities stack in lanes without individual bin addressing per pallet; the strategy manages lane occupancy by product/batch with rules like single-product-per-lane and time-based lane closing.

questions.question: How do capacity checks work in putaway?
questions.answer: Configurable per storage type: by key figures (weight/volume), by bin type vs HU type fit, by maximum HUs per bin, or capacity per product (e.g., liters). Any violation excludes the bin; misconfigured capacity is a top 'no bin found' cause.

questions.question: What are mixed storage settings?
questions.answer: Storage type controls whether different products/batches/HU types may share a bin, and in what combinations. Tight mixed-storage rules improve accuracy but demand more bins; loose rules save space but complicate counting and picking.

questions.question: What is the difference between putaway rules at storage type vs storage section search?
questions.answer: Storage type search picks WHICH type; storage section search then narrows to preferred sections within the type (e.g., heavy section on ground level); bin determination applies the strategy within the section scope.

questions.question: What is HU type dependent putaway?
questions.answer: HU types (Euro, industrial, tote) map to allowed bin types per storage type, so a Euro pallet never targets a half-slot; combined with height checks per bin type for rack safety.

questions.question: How does slotting interact with putaway strategies?
questions.answer: Slotting computes and writes the product's putaway parameters (control indicators, section/bin type preferences, fixed bins); strategies then simply consume better inputs - slotting does not bypass the strategy machinery.

questions.question: What options exist when putaway determination fails at RF?
questions.answer: Exception codes can route to clarification, allow manual bin entry with authorization, or trigger alternative sequences; blocking the operator with no path is a design failure - every flow needs an exception exit.

questions.question: How do you steer hazardous materials putaway?
questions.answer: Hazard ratings/storage classes on the product restrict allowed storage types/sections via checks (fire containment sections, LQ rules); incompatible substance separation is enforced through section and bin restrictions.

questions.question: What is a putaway block vs stock removal block on a bin?
questions.answer: Independent flags: a bin can accept no new stock (putaway block) while still allowing picks, or vice versa - used for maintenance, counts, or phase-outs; both respected by determination, visible in /SCWM/LS03.

questions.question: Explain 'cross-line stock placement' sorting.
questions.answer: The bin sort for putaway alternates across aisles/lines so consecutive putaways spread physically, reducing congestion and equipment queuing at one aisle - different sorting than the picking path.

questions.question: What is the role of the storage bin type check exactly?
questions.answer: Bin type (physical slot class) must be in the allowed list for the HU type being put away; additionally bin-type-specific max weight/height applies. It models 'does this pallet fit this slot' - the most literal capacity rule.

questions.question: When is manual putaway (user decides bin) legitimate?
questions.answer: Clarification handling, unusual items without master data, VIP fast-path decisions by seniors, or fallback during data incidents - always with authorization control and monitored frequency; high manual rates signal broken determination.

questions.question: How does putaway behave for partial HU quantities?
questions.answer: If the putaway quantity is below packspec full-HU levels, quantity classification may route it to case/piece areas instead of reserve; repacking at decon creates suitable putaway HUs - classification thresholds drive the split.

questions.question: What are putaway-relevant settings on the warehouse process type?
questions.answer: Destination determination behavior, confirmation requirements, stock type/availability group defaults, exception code profile, and whether tasks are auto-created at GR - process type mistakes masquerade as strategy bugs.

questions.question: How would you analyze 'wrong storage type chosen' complaints?
questions.answer: Reproduce determination (simulate WT creation), check the product's putaway indicator and slotting values, read the search sequence entries and their conditions, verify earlier types were legitimately excluded (blocks, capacity), and check for process-type-specific sequence overrides.

questions.question: What is the interplay of availability groups with putaway posting changes?
questions.answer: Two-step designs post a change (ROD>AFS) upon final putaway confirmation, often automated via PPF; failures leave stock stored but not sellable - monitor posting-change errors as part of inbound health.

questions.question: Can putaway create multiple WTs from one delivery item? Why?
questions.answer: Yes - palletization splits into HUs, each with its own WT; capacity partial placements and decon outputs also split. One-item-one-task assumptions break reporting and interfaces that were designed naively.

questions.question: What is a 'consolidation group' in putaway/decon context?
questions.answer: A grouping key (typically destination activity area driven) deciding which items may stay together in one HU; decon splits HUs whose items span too many consolidation groups per the allowed number.

questions.question: How does putaway for returns/blocked stock differ?
questions.answer: Separate stock types route to dedicated storage types via sequences filtered by stock type; blocked stock often has restricted areas and no ATP impact - configuration mirrors the quality/blocked process design.

questions.question: What performance considerations exist for putaway determination?
questions.answer: Very long candidate lists (huge types with open sorting), deep capacity checks per bin, and mixed-storage validations cost runtime; healthy designs keep candidate scopes tight and bins/blocks maintained to avoid scanning thousands of bins per task.

questions.question: What is 'storage type role: staging area group' relevance for putaway?
questions.answer: Staging/GI-role types are excluded from standard final putaway; misroled types either wrongly receive stock or block legitimate interim steps - role correctness is part of layout QA.

questions.question: How do you validate a new putaway design before go-live?
questions.answer: Simulation matrix per representative product classes x HU types: verify chosen type/section/bin against design intent, capacity edge cases (overheight/overweight), block behavior, decon relevance, and exception paths - with signed-off evidence.

questions.question: What master data errors most often distort putaway?
questions.answer: Wrong dimensions/weights (capacity misfires), missing putaway indicators after product creation, stale fixed bin flags, absent HU type on packspec levels, and units of measure without conversions.

questions.question: How do 2-step putaway designs (GR zone > final) affect labor and accuracy?
questions.answer: They add a handling touch but enable dock clearing speed, decon quality, and specialization (dock crews vs stacker drivers); accuracy improves via verification at final placement - the trade is throughput vs touches, decided by volume profile.

questions.question: Bins show free in the monitor but determination says full - what do you check?
questions.answer: Open (unconfirmed) WTs reserving destination capacity, HUs logically in the bin without stock (empty HU shells), capacity key figure sums vs bin maxima, blocked status with misleading display filters, and whether a different capacity check (HU count limit) is the binding constraint.

title: Outbound Process: ODO, Staging, Loading, GI

questions.question: Walk through the standard EWM outbound flow.
questions.answer: ERP sales order > outbound delivery distributed to EWM (ODR > ODO) > wave assignment/release > WT creation for picking > pick execution (RF) > packing/VAS as designed > staging to GI zone/staging area > (optional loading onto TU) > goods issue posting > confirmation back to ERP > billing.

questions.question: What data on the ODO drives warehouse behavior?
questions.answer: Warehouse process type per item, route/carrier and departure times, staging area/door determination, wave attributes, quantity classifications, stock type/availability group, and packing relevance - determination happens at document creation from ERP data.

questions.question: What is staging area and door determination outbound?
questions.answer: Rules map route/carrier/departure data to a staging area group/staging area and door, so picked goods stage at the correct dock lane for their truck; wrong determinations misplace freight at the dock.

questions.question: How does EWM handle short picks (stock not available at bin)?
questions.answer: Exception codes at RF (bin empty, damage) trigger alternatives: system re-determines from other bins, creates replenishment, or reduces delivery quantity with a difference reported to ERP - plus a stock investigation task on the source bin.

questions.question: What is pick denial and its process consequences?
questions.answer: The formal rejection of a pick WT quantity via exception: the system logs the denial, may retry determination elsewhere, and flags the bin/product for count. Denial-rate is a core health KPI (data accuracy proxy).

questions.question: What is the difference between picking WT confirmation with and without HU?
questions.answer: Pick-HU processes confirm quantities into a pick handling unit that travels through packing/staging; loose picking confirms quantities to a resource/destination without HU packaging - HU processes give traceability, loose is faster for simple flows.

questions.question: When does packing become a separate step?
questions.answer: When the design requires cartonization, repacking from pick-HUs into shipping HUs, VAS, or quality checks at a packing work center - versus pick-directly-into-shipping-carton designs where the pick HU is the shipment package.

questions.question: What is loading in EWM and when is it modeled?
questions.answer: WTs moving staged HUs onto the TU/door, confirming physical truck loading; modeled when load verification, seal management, or ship-complete controls matter. Simple sites post GI from staging without explicit loading.

questions.question: What checks can block goods issue?
questions.answer: Incomplete picking/packing, open WTs, missing serials/batches, load quantity mismatches, ship-complete rules violated, blocked documents/stock, or interface locks; GI validation is intentionally strict - it is the last gate before legal ownership transfer.

questions.question: What happens system-wise at GI posting?
questions.answer: EWM reduces bin/HU stock, closes the warehouse request, sends the goods movement to ERP (material document, delivery status update), and triggers follow-ons (invoice enablement, proof-of-delivery flows). Errors here split system realities and are severity-1 material.

questions.question: How are outbound cancellations handled after picking but before GI?
questions.answer: Reverse task chains: cancel/reverse pick confirmations returning stock to bins (or via a controlled return-to-stock flow with new putaway), unassign from wave, then adjust or delete the ODO following ERP-side cancellation - sequence discipline prevents stock ghosts.

questions.question: What is 'invoice before goods issue' and where does EWM fit?
questions.answer: Some businesses bill before shipping (prepaid/export cases); process design must ensure EWM GI aligns with already-created billing documents, restricting quantity changes after invoicing - EWM enforces pick-exactness or triggers exception workflows.

questions.question: What is a route in EWM outbound?
questions.answer: The transportation path/schedule abstraction (departure calendar, cutoffs, carrier) used for wave building, staging/door determination, and departure sequencing; routes come from ERP or route determination in EWM designs.

questions.question: How do cutoff times drive the outbound day?
questions.answer: Waves and picking schedules anchor to route departure cutoffs: work is released so picking/packing completes before staging deadlines; missed cutoffs cascade into carrier misses - many escalations are cutoff mathematics.

questions.question: What is ship-complete vs partial shipment control?
questions.answer: Delivery/order-level rules whether partial quantities may ship; EWM must respect them at GI (blocking partial GI where ship-complete) - and support must recognize the resulting 'why can I not GI' tickets as intended control.

questions.question: How does EWM communicate quantity differences at GI to ERP?
questions.answer: Difference quantities adjust the ERP delivery via the confirmation messages (pick denial/short pick outcomes), so billing matches shipped reality; config decides whether differences auto-adjust or need clarification approval.

questions.question: What is 'staging' physically and systemically?
questions.answer: Moving picked/packed HUs to the designated staging area lane for the departure (WT to staging bin); systemically the ODO tracks staging completion per item/HU - the readiness state for loading/GI.

questions.question: What are common causes for 'no staging area/door found'?
questions.answer: Missing determination entries for the route/carrier combination, new doors not mapped to determination groups, TU without proper assignment, or master data (departure calendar) gaps - mirrored by our cold-chain door incident pattern.

questions.question: What is a shipping cockpit/TU-centric outbound?
questions.answer: Work revolves around transportation units: assign deliveries to TUs, monitor readiness per TU, load and depart TUs - useful for multi-delivery truckloads; EWM shipping cockpit transactions/monitor nodes support this view.

questions.question: How do serial numbers affect outbound?
questions.answer: Serial capture/validation at pick, pack, or GI per profile; GI blocks on missing/mismatched serials. High-serialization flows need scanning ergonomics and clean status alignment with ERP equipment records to avoid GI failures.

questions.question: What is the role of PPF outbound?
questions.answer: Printing (pick lists, HU labels, delivery notes, carrier labels), messaging (GI notifications, ASN to customers), and internal follow-ons - condition-triggered at document events; failed outbound PPF equals missing paperwork tickets.

questions.question: What KPIs define outbound health?
questions.answer: On-time-ship rate vs cutoffs, pick productivity and denial rate, order cycle time (release-to-GI), staging accuracy, GI failure rate, and same-day backlog carryover - monitored per shift with the monitor + BI extracts.

questions.question: How would you approach a 'truck waiting, cannot GI' severity call?
questions.answer: Fast triage in the ODO: which status blocks (open WTs? serials? load mismatch?) - fix the specific gate (confirm/cancel stragglers, resolve serials, correct assignment), avoid data-forcing without understanding, communicate ETA, and document for the post-mortem. The incident guide's stock-mismatch case is the deep variant.

questions.question: What is wave vs waveless (immediate) outbound processing?
questions.answer: Waves batch demand for efficiency (consolidated picking, resource leveling); waveless releases WTs immediately per order (speed for e-commerce). Many sites mix: waves for scheduled routes, immediate for express - process type/wave attributes steer it.

questions.question: What is cartonization planning?
questions.answer: Pre-calculating shipping cartons (number/size, item-to-carton assignment) before picking - enabling pick-to-carton flows and carrier label at pick; advanced feature relying on accurate cube data and packspecs.

questions.question: How do you reprint a lost pick list or HU label correctly?
questions.answer: Via the document/HU output actions (repeat PPF processing) rather than OS-level spool copies, so reprints are logged and条 content reflects current document state; uncontrolled reprints breed duplicate-label incidents like our HU case.

questions.question: What is the two-step picking concept?
questions.answer: Step 1 picks total quantities per product into a consolidation zone (batch pick), step 2 distributes to orders - efficient when many orders share few SKUs; EWM supports it via specific process design with withdrawal and distribution tasks.

questions.question: How does EWM support kit-to-order outbound?
questions.answer: Kit headers explode into components on the ODO with a linked VAS work order at a kitting work center; components pick to the kit build, finished kits pack/ship - hierarchy fields must arrive correctly (see incident 21).

questions.question: What loading validations can EWM enforce?
questions.answer: Scan-verify each HU onto the correct TU/door, completeness checks per delivery/TU, sequence loading (drop order), seal number capture, and weight totals vs vehicle limits where configured - configurable per process rigor.

questions.question: Order stuck 'in wave, no WTs created' - the usual suspects?
questions.answer: Wave locked/not released, WT creation errors at release (no stock, determination failures - check wave/task creation logs), item without wave assignment due to attribute gaps, or a background job failure for the release itself - the wave log tells the story.

questions.question: What determines the stock removal search sequence?
questions.answer: The stock removal control indicator from the warehouse product plus process/quantity data map to a search sequence in customizing: an ordered list of storage types (optionally with quantity classification splits) to search for available stock.

questions.question: Name the standard removal rules within a storage type.
questions.answer: FIFO (oldest GR date first), LIFO, FEFO/shelf-life (earliest expiry), quantity fit strategies (smallest/largest quantities first to clean partials or minimize touches), fixed bin first, and options sorting like preferring emptied bins.

questions.question: How does FEFO get enforced end-to-end?
questions.answer: Batch-managed product with SLED, removal rule sorting by expiry, plus GR-side minimum shelf-life checks and customer-specific remaining-shelf-life requirements (batch determination); support cases arise when customer rules exceed available shelf life.

questions.question: What is quantity classification's role in removal?
questions.answer: Requested quantities classify (pallet/case/piece via packspec thresholds), and the search sequence can branch per class - full pallets from reserve, cases from case-pick, pieces from piece-pick - optimizing touches and stock hygiene.

questions.question: What is rounding in stock removal?
questions.answer: Rounding quantities to packspec units (whole cartons/pallets) where business allows: over/under-delivery tolerances feed rounding rules to avoid breaking pack units for marginal quantities - reducing repack labor.

questions.question: Explain 'stringent FIFO' vs pragmatic sequences.
questions.answer: Strict FIFO across the whole warehouse can force uneconomic picks (one old case far away); pragmatic designs apply FIFO within the type searched first by efficiency logic. Regulated goods may mandate strict enforcement - a design decision to surface explicitly.

questions.question: What causes 'no stock found' during WT creation despite monitor showing stock?
questions.answer: Stock in non-searched storage types (sequence gap), wrong stock type (Q/blocked vs unrestricted), locks by other tasks/waves, batch restrictions (expiry, status), quantity classification pointing to an empty area, or stock reserved by open documents.

questions.question: How do batch determination criteria integrate outbound?
questions.answer: Customer/order batch selection criteria (origin, shelf life, characteristics) filter eligible batches before removal determination; EWM respects the delivery's batch or selects per criteria - mismatches produce 'stock exists but not usable' cases.

questions.question: What is a 'negative stock' situation in removal contexts?
questions.answer: Certain interim bins may allow temporary negative quantities (e.g., production supply staging with timing offsets) if configured; uncontrolled negatives elsewhere signal confirmation sequence errors - monitor and clear them daily.

questions.question: How does the system pick between multiple bins with equal rule ranking?
questions.answer: Tie-breakers: sort by bin sorting sequence within the activity area, bin access optimization, or additional sort fields (GR date, quantity); deterministic tie-breaking matters for test reproducibility.

questions.question: What is 'pick from staging/cross-docking' opportunistically?
questions.answer: Cross-docking designs let outbound demand consume inbound stock still at GR/staging (before putaway), skipping storage touches; requires activation and matching windows - powerful for flow-through DCs.

questions.question: What are removal-relevant HU behaviors?
questions.answer: Full-HU withdrawal (take whole pallet when quantity matches/rounds to it), partial withdrawal creating a rest-HU, and HU-neutral loose picks; strategy plus packspec decide, affecting how many touches and rest-stock fragments arise.

questions.question: What is replenishment's relationship with removal strategies?
questions.answer: Pick faces are removal targets for case/piece classes; replenishment (planned/order-related/automatic) keeps them stocked. Denials in pick faces usually indict replenishment timing/parameters rather than the removal rule itself.

questions.question: Explain order-related (demand-driven) replenishment.
questions.answer: Triggered by open pick demand exceeding pick-face stock at WT creation/wave release: the system generates replenishment WTs just-in-time for the shortfall - minimizing standing pick-face inventory at the cost of pick-wave latency.

questions.question: When would 'largest quantity first' removal make sense?
questions.answer: To empty bulk/reserve bins fastest (fewer partial pallets), for space recovery goals, or to minimize task count for big demands - traded against FIFO strictness and freshness rules.

questions.question: How do stock removal blocks and bin blocks interplay?
questions.answer: Removal-blocked bins are skipped by determination even with eligible stock; support must distinguish 'no stock' from 'stock present but removal-blocked' - the monitor shows blocks, tickets often do not mention them.

questions.question: What is 'stock transfer between availability groups' during outbound?
questions.answer: Some designs stage via posting changes (e.g., AFS to a GI-staging availability group/sloc) so ERP mirrors dock stock; failures leave ERP/EWM split - the mechanism behind the classic GI stock-determination incident.

questions.question: How are alternative units handled in removal quantities?
questions.answer: Requested UoM converts via product conversions; packspec-classified thresholds evaluate in base UoM - broken conversions produce misclassification (piece demand treated as pallets) with bizarre bin choices as the visible symptom.

questions.question: What debugging approach do you take for wrong-bin proposals?
questions.answer: Recreate via WT simulation, then walk the determination log: control indicator > sequence > per-type rule > candidate list with exclusion reasons (locks/blocks/capacity/batch) - the log names the culprit; guessing without it wastes hours.

questions.question: What is 'combined picking' of identical products across orders?
questions.answer: Wave/WOCR designs can bundle same-product tasks (pick total then distribute - two-step) or sequence same-bin visits consecutively; reduces bin visits at the cost of downstream distribution effort.

questions.question: Physical stock exists, monitor agrees, yet the specific wave locked it elsewhere - explain.
questions.answer: Wave release creates WTs reserving the stock; later documents find it locked. Competing demand designs need prioritization rules and possibly stock segmentation - explain reservation mechanics to the business rather than 'freeing' stock ad hoc.

questions.question: What is the emptying-bins preference and its benefit?
questions.answer: Prefer bins whose stock will be fully consumed by the pick (emptied), releasing bins faster for putaway and keeping the warehouse defragmented - valuable in tight-capacity operations.

questions.question: How do you handle picking from bulk lanes with LIFO physics?
questions.answer: Bulk stacks are physically LIFO (front/top accessible); configure LIFO or lane-based logic for bulk types even under FIFO policy elsewhere, or accept re-handling costs - policy vs physics must be reconciled in design.

questions.question: What role do storage groups for removal ('bin access types') play?
questions.answer: They ensure only resources/equipment able to reach a bin get its tasks (crane zones vs ground bins); wrong access config strands tasks in queues no resource can serve.

questions.question: What is interleaving and its benefit?
questions.answer: Mixing task types for a resource (putaway on the way back from a pick - task interleaving) to cut deadhead travel; enabled via queue design and resource management semantics - measurable double-digit travel savings in large DCs.

questions.question: Removal strategy changes went live and pick paths degraded sharply - what likely got missed?
questions.answer: Activity area bin sorting for the newly targeted storage types (execution order), WOCR compatibility (order sizes), and queue mappings - determination changed WHERE, but nobody re-tuned the WHERE's execution layer.

questions.question: How does two-depth or double-deep racking affect removal?
questions.answer: Rear positions depend on front positions being cleared; bin access/strategy must respect pairing (front-first retrieval, shuffling tasks), often via bin type design and custom access logic - otherwise unreachable-task deadlocks appear.

questions.question: What is a 'stock removal control indicator' review cycle?
questions.answer: Periodic (with slotting) validation that each product's indicator matches current demand pattern (a former fast mover still routed to piece-pick), preventing strategy drift as assortments change.

questions.question: Which logs/monitors reveal removal problems fastest?
questions.answer: WT creation logs (simulation), wave release logs, the ODO item status with its determination messages, denial/exception analysis nodes, and pick-face stock-vs-min reports - correlated, they isolate strategy vs stock vs execution causes.

questions.question: Design question: e-commerce singles vs retail pallet outbound in one warehouse - removal architecture?
questions.answer: Separate quantity-class branches: piece demand to a dedicated piece-pick area (waveless, batch-pick with put-walls), case/pallet demand via case-pick and reserve with waves per route; shared reserve replenishes both - one sequence, class-differentiated branches, distinct WOCR/queues per stream.

questions.question: What is a wave in EWM?
questions.answer: A grouping of warehouse request items released together for picking - batching demand to optimize resource usage, sequence work against cutoffs, and consolidate related orders (route, carrier, area).

questions.question: What are wave templates?
questions.answer: Configuration objects defining how waves form: assignment conditions (route, departure, process type), capacity limits (items, weight, volume, tasks), release method and times, and options like automatic WT creation and 2-step relevance.

questions.question: How do delivery items get assigned to waves?
questions.answer: Automatically at ODO creation via wave determination (condition technique against template attributes) or manually/by report; items carry wave assignment until release generates WTs.

questions.question: What is wave release and what happens technically?
questions.answer: Release triggers WT creation for all assigned items (per strategies), locks relevant stock, creates WOs per WOCR, and pushes work to queues - the moment planning becomes executable work; its log records every failure.

questions.question: Name wave release methods.
