questions.answer: Immediate (at assignment), scheduled (release time/job), and manual - plus automatic release variants driven by capacity fill or time triggers depending on release.

questions.question: What is wave capacity control good for?
questions.answer: Caps (weight/volume/items/WTs) keep released work digestible per period, protecting packing/staging from floods and leveling labor - waves sized to takt rather than to whatever demand arrived.

questions.question: What are wave types/attributes used for operationally?
questions.answer: Distinguishing behavior classes: express vs standard, store replenishment vs e-com, with different templates, priorities, and monitor filters - making exception handling and reporting stream-aware.

questions.question: What is a wave 'lock' and when does it appear?
questions.answer: During processing (release/change), waves lock against parallel edits; stuck locks (crashed jobs) block release/changes - support clears them per lock-entry analysis, never blindly.

questions.question: How do 2-step picking waves work?
questions.answer: The wave marks items 2-step relevant: release creates withdrawal (batch) tasks first; after consolidation, distribution tasks allocate to orders - wave options plus process config coordinate the pair.

questions.question: What belongs in a wave release failure triage?
questions.answer: Read the wave log: per-item failure reasons (no stock, determination errors, locks) - fix causes, re-release the failed subset, and monitor completion vs cutoff; parallel: assess whether partial release plus manual expediting protects the departure.

questions.question: Why can a wave stay in 'released' with unfinished WTs invisible to the floor?
questions.answer: Queue misdetermination (tasks routed to unserved queues), WOCR left tasks in unassigned states, RF filters hiding queues, or resource group gaps - work exists but no one is subscribed to it (compare the RF no-work incident).

questions.question: What is wave completion and its downstream effect?
questions.answer: All WTs confirmed: the wave completes, enabling staging/GI progression and template-based follow-ons; monitoring watches completion percentage against departure countdown as THE outbound heartbeat.

questions.question: How do priorities work between waves?
questions.answer: Queue sequencing plus WO priority derived from wave/route urgency order the floor's work; express waves preempt via higher priority queues or dedicated resources - design decides preemption vs dedicated lanes.

questions.question: When is automatic wave assignment risky?
questions.answer: Attribute data quality issues (routes/departures wrong) misgroup orders; late order changes after assignment strand items; over-broad conditions build mega-waves - guard with validation reports and capacity caps.

questions.question: What is a 'pick wave' vs 'load wave' thinking?
questions.answer: Some operations wave by picking efficiency, others by load/departure structure; EWM templates can layer both (wave per route-departure with capacity splits) - the framing controls dock flow smoothness.

questions.question: How would you handle 3,800-item promo waves (from the incident)?
questions.answer: Split via capacity limits into sequential sub-waves, stagger release times, parallelize by area attributes, and pre-scale packing/staging labor - plus job/runtime settings able to handle release volume (the incident's technical layer).

questions.question: What reporting exists on waves?
questions.answer: Monitor wave nodes (status, item counts, completion), release logs, and BI/queries on wave cycle times (assignment-to-release-to-completion) - feeding cutoff risk dashboards.

questions.question: Can items leave a wave after release?
questions.answer: Released items with created WTs must be handled via task cancellation and wave removal actions; discipline matters - orphan half-released items cause GI blockers later. Pre-release removal is trivial by comparison.

questions.question: What is subsystem-relevant wave logic (WCS/MFS)?
questions.answer: Waves feeding automation must respect equipment capacity (station rates); release floods overwhelm buffers - templates throttle by automation takt, or MFS-side flow control compensates.

questions.question: Wave assignment works in QA, fails in prod for one route - suspicion order?
questions.answer: Missing condition records for the route in prod, route/departure master data divergence, template transport gaps, and time zone/calendar differences affecting departure derivation - compare determination inputs side by side.

questions.question: What are wave 'options' worth knowing cold?
questions.answer: Automatic WT creation at release, WO creation timing, 2-step flags, replenishment triggering at release, and template-level log/alert behavior - each toggles a support-relevant behavior.

questions.question: How do cutoff changes propagate to waves?
questions.answer: Departure/route changes re-derive wave attributes only per design - often requiring re-assignment runs; silent non-propagation after transport-plan changes is a recurring gotcha producing wrong release times.

questions.question: What is your position on manual waves in steady state?
questions.answer: Acceptable for exceptions (recovery, VIP orders); chronic manual waving signals broken determination or templates - measure manual share and drive it down via config fixes.

questions.question: How do waves interact with replenishment timing?
questions.answer: Order-related replenishment can trigger at release - meaning pick-face refill tasks race picking; sequencing (replenishment queues prioritized, lead offsets) prevents pickers arriving before stock does.

questions.question: Why monitor 'unassigned delivery items' as a daily job?
questions.answer: Items that missed wave determination (attribute gaps) will never release - silent order sleepers; a daily report catching unassigned outbound items before cutoff is a standard support safeguard.

questions.question: What does wave simulation offer?
questions.answer: Testing template conditions/capacities against real demand without execution - previewing wave composition for new templates or peak plans; underused but valuable in change management.

questions.question: How do you size wave windows against packing capacity?
questions.answer: Wave size x pick rate defines arrival curve at packing; align released units per hour with packing takt (stations x rate), buffering peaks via staged releases - waves are the valve, packing the constraint.

questions.question: One wave per truck or several - trade-offs?
questions.answer: Per-truck waves simplify staging/loading traceability; multiple smaller waves smooth labor and shorten feedback loops but need disciplined staging consolidation - volume and dock layout decide.

questions.question: What authorization/oversight applies to wave release actions?
questions.answer: Release/cancel rights restricted to leads; log review responsibilities defined; release-time changes under change control during peak - waves steer the whole outbound engine, so their controls match that criticality.

questions.question: Waveless operations claim they do not need wave skills - your take for interviews?
questions.answer: Even immediate-release designs use the same machinery (determination, WT creation, logs) - just with instant timing; understanding waves means understanding outbound release mechanics, which every EWM consultant needs for triage.

questions.question: Define warehouse task precisely.
questions.answer: The elementary executable instruction to move a quantity (product WT) or an HU (HU WT) from a source to a destination, carrying process type, quantities, stock attributes, exception options, and confirmation requirements.

questions.question: Define warehouse order precisely.
questions.answer: The work package assigned to one resource at a time, bundling WTs per creation rules with sorting, limits, and packing profile - the unit a picker actually receives on RF.

questions.question: What are warehouse order creation rules (WOCR)?
questions.answer: Configurable rules that filter, sort, split, and limit WTs into WOs (item caps, weight/volume/time limits, consolidation groups, sort profiles), searched in a defined sequence per activity area/process.

questions.question: Why do WOCR limits use execution time estimates?
questions.answer: Time limits build WOs of even labor content (e.g., 20-minute orders) using engineered standards - fairer than item counts across heterogeneous tasks and the basis for takt-stable operations.

questions.question: What is a consolidation group in WOCR context?
questions.answer: A key controlling which items may share a WO/pick-HU (same destination staging lane/customer compatibility); it prevents mixing freight that must stay separate.

questions.question: What happens to WTs that no WOCR rule accepts?
questions.answer: They land in a leftover/default WO per the rule sequence's catch-all behavior - functional but unoptimized; monitoring catch-all volume reveals rule coverage gaps (our oversized-WO incident pattern).

questions.question: Explain WT confirmation variants.
questions.answer: Foreground RF (scan-verify source/destination/quantity), background (system-posted for automation/trusted flows), with or without exceptions, and pick-HU integrated confirmation - process type plus storage type settings decide the rigor.

questions.question: What is alternate confirmation ('confirm with difference')?
questions.answer: Confirming less/more than target with exception codes documenting why (short pick, overage) - triggering follow-ons (difference postings, denials, investigations) rather than silently wrong quantities.

questions.question: What is a 'blocked' WT and its usual causes?
questions.answer: Tasks not executable: locked stock, blocked bins, wave locks, or explicit user blocks; monitor filters expose them - aged blocked tasks are housekeeping debt (see orphaned-WT incident).

questions.question: How do you safely cancel a confirmed WT?
questions.answer: Confirmed product WTs are history - correction happens via reverse movements (new WT back) or stock corrections, not cancellation; only unconfirmed tasks cancel cleanly. Interviewers test this asymmetry.

questions.question: What is task interleaving at the WO level?
questions.answer: Resource management can hand a putaway WO after a pick WO in the same area (travel pairing) via queue design; WOs stay single-purpose but sequencing interleaves - distinguishing concept from configuration reality.

questions.question: What is the WO status lifecycle?
questions.answer: Open (created, queue-assigned) > in process (resource selected/started) > confirmed (all WTs done); plus waiting/blocked variants; monitors aggregate these into floor progress views.

questions.question: How does system-guided RF pick the next WO?
questions.answer: By queue sequence of the resource group, then priority, then sorting (e.g., LSD - latest start date) within queue - configuration decides; 'why did he get THAT order' tickets resolve by replaying this chain.

questions.question: What are packing profiles in WOCR?
questions.answer: Rules generating pick-HUs for WOs (how many, which packaging material, item-to-HU distribution via packspec/cube logic) so pickers receive prepared cartons/totes for pick-to-pack designs.

questions.question: What is a 'bin denial' vs 'quantity reduction' at confirmation?
questions.answer: Bin denial reports the bin unusable (empty/damaged) rerouting the full demand; quantity reduction confirms partial with a difference for the remainder - different exception codes, different follow-on chains.

questions.question: When are HU WTs used vs product WTs?
questions.answer: HU WTs move whole handling units (pallet putaway, staging moves, decon routing); product WTs move quantities (picks, replenishment); POSC steps typically chain HU WTs while picking generates product WTs into HUs.

questions.question: What sorting decides WT sequence within a WO?
questions.answer: The activity area's bin sort sequence for the activity, refined by WOCR sort profiles; the printed/RF sequence equals travel path - wrong sorting silently costs minutes per order.

questions.question: How do priorities flow from documents to tasks?
questions.answer: Delivery/route urgency derives wave priority, which passes to WOs/queues; manual priority overrides exist for expediting - governed, logged, and used sparingly.

questions.question: What are 'open WT' aging reports for?
questions.answer: Aged unconfirmed tasks signal stuck flows (lost paper, abandoned RF sessions, blocked bins); daily review with thresholds per process keeps execution debt near zero - a core support routine.

questions.question: Explain 'WT simulation' as a support tool.
questions.answer: Simulating task creation for a delivery item without posting shows determination outcomes and logs (strategies, exclusions) - the fastest root-cause tool for 'wrong bin/no bin' analysis.

questions.question: What is the role of exception codes on WT operations?
questions.answer: They encode deviations (denial, damage, bin overflow) with configured follow-ons (stock investigation, rerouting, alerts) and analytics - turning floor problems into structured system events.

questions.question: Which WOCR mistakes create the most floor pain?
questions.answer: Missing limits (monster WOs), wrong consolidation grouping (mixed incompatible freight), bad sort profiles (zigzag paths), and sequence errors letting catch-alls win - each maps to a measurable KPI dip.

questions.question: How does WO assignment interact with position management?
questions.answer: Multi-position resources (pick carts) map WO pick-HUs to cart positions, guiding put sequences; misconfigured positions produce confused RF dialogs - niche but interview-worthy.

questions.question: Can one WT belong to multiple WOs or waves?
questions.answer: No - a WT belongs to at most one WO and one wave context; regrouping requires removing/canceling and recreating; understanding this containment hierarchy (wave > WO > WT) prevents wrong fix attempts.

questions.question: What logs exist for WT creation failures at wave release?
questions.answer: The wave release log per item plus application log entries; they name determination failures (no stock, no bin) precisely - support reads logs before touching config, always.

questions.question: How do you mass-process tasks safely in production?
questions.answer: Monitor-based mass actions (confirm/cancel) with strict filters, small verified batches, floor confirmation of physical reality, documented evidence, and four-eyes for destructive actions - mass tools amplify both fixes and mistakes.

questions.question: What is 'queue jumping' and when is it acceptable?
questions.answer: Manually reassigning WOs/resources to expedite specific work; acceptable in escalations under lead approval - chronic queue jumping indicates broken priority design and destroys planning credibility.

questions.question: What data would you pull for a pick productivity analysis?
questions.answer: WT/WO confirmation timestamps and quantities per resource/area, travel estimates vs actuals, denial/exception frequencies, and WO size distributions - identifying whether losses sit in waiting, travel, or handling.

questions.question: Why can a WO sit unassigned though resources are free?
questions.answer: Queue not in any active resource group sequence, resource logged into different queues, WO waiting on preceding steps (POSC), blocked tasks inside, or priority starvation by design - enumerate, verify, fix.

questions.question: Explain the ideal division of labor between waves, WOCR, and queues.
questions.answer: Waves decide WHEN demand releases; WOCR decides HOW work packages look; queues decide WHO gets them; keeping these concerns separated in design keeps each independently tunable - the hallmark of a maintainable EWM.

questions.question: Define process-oriented storage control (POSC).
questions.answer: A configured sequence of process steps (external steps like unload, count, decon, VAS, putaway) that goods pass through per storage process assigned via the process type - each step generating its own task legs and work center visits as needed.

questions.question: Define layout-oriented storage control (LOSC).
questions.answer: Routing rules forcing movements between two points to pass intermediate locations (I-points, conveyors handover bins, elevators) based on layout constraints - the physical topology layer under process steps.

questions.question: How do POSC and LOSC combine?
questions.answer: POSC defines the logical step chain; LOSC refines each leg's physical path where layout demands (a putaway step whose leg to the high bay passes the I-point). They are complementary, not alternatives.

questions.question: What is a storage process definition?
questions.answer: The customizing object listing external process steps in sequence with their behavior (work center determination, HU relevance, automatic vs manual) - assigned inbound via process type or delivery, outbound analogously.

questions.question: What are external vs internal process steps?
questions.answer: External steps are the modeled milestones (DECON, VAS, PACK); internal steps are system-known standard operations mapped underneath - customers name external steps freely, mapping each to internal semantics.

questions.question: How does the system decide a step is 'relevant' or skippable?
questions.answer: Relevance logic per step: configuration plus runtime checks (decon only for mixed HUs crossing consolidation-group limits, VAS only when a VAS order exists) - irrelevant steps skip automatically, keeping flows lean.

questions.question: Where do intermediate destinations of steps come from?
questions.answer: Step configuration assigns work centers/storage sections or determination logic picks concrete bins (work center determination per consolidation group, staging determination) - each step leg needs a resolvable destination or tasks fail.

questions.question: What generates the movement between steps?
questions.answer: Confirmation of one step's WT triggers creation of the next leg's task per the chain (HU-based typically), until final destination; a break mid-chain leaves HUs stranded at interim bins - the classic 'HU stuck at decon' symptom.

questions.question: Diagnose: HUs stuck at a POSC step with no follow-on task.
questions.answer: Check step config for the next step's determination (work center/bin resolvable?), HU state (blocked? mixed relevance changed?), queue of the follow-on tasks, and application log at last confirmation - usually a determination-gap after layout/master data changes.

questions.question: What is the pick point role in LOSC outbound?
questions.answer: Retrieval from automated storage passes a pick point where partial quantities are taken; remainder returns - LOSC forces the routing; work center config governs the pick point handling.

questions.question: How does storage control interact with MFS?
questions.answer: Automation legs (conveyor segments) are LOSC-routed communication points where MFS takes over task execution via telegrams; storage control defines the handover topology between manual and automated realms.

questions.question: Why not model every physical touch as a POSC step?
questions.answer: Each step adds tasks, confirmations, and failure surface; model only where control/visibility pays (quality gates, labor tracking, routing decisions) - overmodeling produces fragile, slow flows and support burden.

questions.question: What is a handover bin/zone and its master data?
questions.answer: Interim bins with appropriate storage type roles at step boundaries (decon inbound buffer, conveyor infeed); they must exist, be determined, and be monitored for accumulation - physical lanes mirrored 1:1 in the system.

questions.question: Outbound POSC: typical step chains?
questions.answer: Pick > (pack at work center) > (VAS) > staging > loading > GI; packing/VAS steps route pick-HUs via work centers per relevance; staging determination sets the final pre-loading destination.

questions.question: How is a work center determined for a step at runtime?
questions.answer: Via step configuration (fixed) or determination by consolidation group/section mapping - balancing station load may need custom logic; failed determination equals stranded HUs, monitored via step backlog nodes.

questions.question: What changes storage-control-wise when adding a new VAS station?
questions.answer: Create work center + bins, extend step's work center determination (consolidation groups), adjust queues/printer determination for the station, and test relevance logic end-to-end - config, master data, and execution layers all touched.

questions.question: What is 'process-oriented' about inbound counting steps?
questions.answer: Counting as a step (post-unload verification at a count work center) inserts a quality gate before putaway for selected flows (new vendors, damage history) - relevance rules target risk-based counting rather than blanket checks.

questions.question: Can process steps differ per product within one delivery?
questions.answer: Yes - relevance evaluates per HU/item context (only mixed HUs decon; only VAS-relevant items route to VAS), so one delivery's HUs may take different paths - by design, confusing only if undocumented.

questions.question: How do you visualize/monitor step backlogs?
questions.answer: Warehouse monitor nodes per interim storage types/work centers (stock/HUs sitting per step), open task lists filtered by step queues, and dwell-time analysis - each step boundary is a measurable buffer.

questions.question: What are frequent POSC transport/cutover failures?
questions.answer: Step chains referencing work centers/bins not migrated, determination tables partially transported, relevance behaving differently due to missing consolidation groups - end-to-end flow tests in production hypercare catch them (cold-door incident analog).

questions.question: What is the difference between storage process for inbound vs outbound assignment?
questions.answer: Inbound: storage process assigned via warehouse process type of the inbound item. Outbound: steps derive from process type plus packing/staging/loading configuration - both land in the same step execution machinery.

questions.question: How would you retrofit a deconsolidation step into a live warehouse?
questions.answer: Config in QA (step insertion, relevance, work center determination), regression-test unaffected flows (must skip the step), floor readiness (station, labor, printers), transport in a low-volume window with fallback plan, and hypercare monitoring of step backlog and dock-to-stock KPI.

questions.question: What role do HU types play in storage control routing?
questions.answer: Conveyability and station compatibility: non-conveyable HU types route around automation legs, oversized HUs to floor paths - routing rules keyed on HU type keep physical reality enforced.

questions.question: Explain 'automatic' steps.
questions.answer: Steps confirmed by the system without user action (background confirmations at telegram events, auto-posting changes) - reducing labor for control-only milestones; failure monitoring replaces human eyes there.

questions.question: A step's work center is overloaded - what system levers exist?
questions.answer: Determination spreading across parallel stations (consolidation-group remapping), relevance tightening (fewer HUs route there), queue re-prioritization, and takt-aligned wave throttling upstream - plus the physical option: more stations.

questions.question: What is the relation between staging area determination and outbound storage control?
questions.answer: Staging determination resolves the final staging destination used by the staging step's tasks; broken determination breaks the last chain leg - trucks miss freight not because picking failed but because staging legs errored.

questions.question: Why are POSC flows sensitive to HU merges/splits mid-process?
questions.answer: Steps track HUs; repacking mid-chain changes the tracked objects - follow-on determination must re-evaluate (new consolidation groups), and poorly-placed repacks orphan step chains; design keeps repacking at defined stations only.

questions.question: How do you explain POSC value to a business stakeholder?
questions.answer: Each step is a control gate with data: where freight is, how long each stage takes, where bottlenecks form - the cost of extra confirmations buys process visibility and enforced quality gates measurable in KPI dashboards.

questions.question: What testing approach fits storage control changes?
questions.answer: Scenario-matrix testing: HU types x relevance conditions x destinations, walking each chain to final confirmation in QA, including negative tests (forced determination failures) verifying error handling - plus volume tests where automation is involved.

questions.question: Interview classic: goods must pass quality inspection only for flagged vendors - solution sketch?
questions.answer: Inbound POSC with a counting/inspection step whose relevance derives from vendor/QM data (inspection rule creating quality stock or a step-relevance check), routing flagged receipts via the QI work center, others straight to putaway - config-first, custom relevance logic only if standard checks cannot express the rule.

questions.question: What is the EWM RF framework?
questions.answer: The runtime and development environment for radio-frequency (mobile scanner) transactions: screen flows optimized for barcode work, verification handling, exception integration, and device-agnostic rendering (ITSmobile/browser).

questions.question: How do users connect to RF?
questions.answer: Via /SCWM/RFUI (GUI or ITSmobile-rendered on devices); logon selects warehouse, resource, and presentation profile - resource assignment links the human/equipment to queues and work.

questions.question: What is the presentation device concept?
questions.answer: Device profiles define screen size/format so one RF logic renders on different hardware (handheld, truck-mounted, wrist) - format groups map screens per device class.

questions.question: What is system-guided vs user-directed RF work?
questions.answer: System-guided: the system pushes the optimal next WO from subscribed queues. User-directed: workers select/scan specific work (by WO, HU, bin). Guided maximizes optimization; directed serves exceptions and specialized roles.

questions.question: How does verification work in RF flows?
questions.answer: Each critical field (bin, product, HU, quantity) can require scan/entry verification against expected values (configurable verification profiles); wrong scans block confirmation - the accuracy backbone of RF operations.

questions.question: What are RF exception codes UX-wise?
questions.answer: Function keys/menu options presenting allowed exceptions per screen/step (bin empty, HU damaged, skip); each triggers its configured chain - the picker's structured escape hatches.

questions.question: How do you add a custom RF screen/flow cleanly?
questions.answer: Via the RF framework's wizard/customizing: copy standard navigation, add steps/screens with framework services (validation, function key mapping), keep logic in framework classes - never hack ITS templates directly; upgrade-safety comes from framework discipline.

questions.question: What is the logical transaction concept in RF?
questions.answer: RF flows are modeled as logical transactions with steps and state - enabling resume after disconnection: the user returns to the exact step; sessions survive network blips by design.

questions.question: A device shows frozen/stale RF session - standard remedy?
questions.answer: Terminate the hung session (SM04/resource management), let the user re-logon and resume the logical transaction; investigate network/device if recurring - and check for locks left by the dead session on tasks/HUs.

questions.question: What is a resource in execution terms?
questions.answer: The logged-on work unit (user+equipment) holding WOs, positions, and queue subscriptions; execution monitoring shows per-resource current task, idle times, and last confirmations - the labor-visibility anchor.

questions.question: How does the queue sequence of a resource group work?
questions.answer: An ordered queue list per group: system-guided selection scans queues in order and serves the best WO per priority/sorting; sequence order implements area/type preferences per workforce segment.

questions.question: What are typical causes of 'no work found' at RF?
questions.answer: Resource group without the right queues (our incident), all matching WOs blocked/in-process, priority/sorting filtering everything out, or WO-resource incompatibilities (bin access, HU type) - reproducible via execution monitor comparison.

questions.question: What is semi-system-guided work?
questions.answer: The user picks the queue, system picks the WO within it - a middle mode for supervisors steering areas while keeping in-queue optimization.

questions.question: How is equipment capability enforced (forklift vs picker)?
questions.answer: Resource types with bin access types and HU type compatibility filter eligible tasks; queues typically align with equipment classes - preventing a foot picker receiving high-rack pallet tasks.

questions.question: What ergonomics/settings reduce RF errors measurably?
questions.answer: Check-digit verification on bins, product scans over descriptions, short screens with single actions, exception keys visible, quantity confirmation only when deviating - configuration choices with measurable error-rate impact.

questions.question: What is RF 'recovery' after device crash mid-confirmation?
questions.answer: The logical transaction state persists: re-logon offers resuming the open WO/step; incomplete confirmations remain unposted, tasks locked by the resource may need supervisor release - documented recovery SOP is part of go-live readiness.

questions.question: How would you monitor RF performance issues systematically?
questions.answer: Correlate: response-time traces (ST12) on RF function modules, network health for the device fleet (WLAN survey data), session counts, and specific slow steps (which screen) - separating system, network, and device causes (compare the performance incident).

questions.question: What is the execution monitor's value for supervisors?
questions.answer: Live view of resources: who works what, idle spans, last confirmations, queue backlogs - enabling real-time rebalancing (moving people between queues) with data instead of walking the floor blind.

questions.question: Can RF work offline?
questions.answer: Standard EWM RF requires connectivity (server round-trips per step); offline needs third-party/custom buffering solutions with sync risks - the honest answer is: design robust WLAN instead.

questions.question: What are RF menu/role design principles?
questions.answer: Role-based menus (picker sees picking only), minimal navigation depth, consistent function keys across flows, and language/terminology matching the floor - training cost and error rates follow menu design quality.

questions.question: How do RF and printing interact at pick/pack?
questions.answer: Confirmations trigger PPF outputs (labels at station printers via printer determination); RF users need clear feedback when print fails - a silent print failure becomes a downstream mystery, so status surfaces matter (printer incidents).

questions.question: What is the role of position management for cart picking?
questions.answer: Multi-order carts map pick-HUs to physical cart positions; RF directs 'put to position 3' - enabling batch-cart flows with put-accuracy; setup spans WOCR packing profiles, positions, and RF dialogs.

questions.question: What authorization concepts apply to RF users?
questions.answer: Beyond roles for transactions: warehouse/resource-level restrictions, exception code authorizations (who may deny/adjust), and supervisor functions (unlocking, reassigned) separated from operator profiles - least privilege on the floor too.

questions.question: How do you roll out an RF flow change with minimal disruption?
questions.answer: Pilot queue/area with selected users, parallel old flow fallback, floor-side quick reference cards, hypercare presence at shift start, and rollback transport ready - RF changes touch muscle memory, so change management equals config quality.

questions.question: Interview scenario: pickers complain the system sends them across the warehouse randomly - analysis path?
questions.answer: Verify activity area bin sorting (execution order), WOCR sort profile, queue-to-area alignment (one queue spanning distant areas causes jumps), interleaving effects, and whether system-guided selection crosses queues by sequence design - then quantify travel from confirmation timestamps and fix the guilty layer.

questions.question: Which transaction maintains resources?
questions.answer: /SCWM/RSRC for resource maintenance; resource groups and their queue sequences live in resource management settings; the execution monitor shows live resource status.

questions.question: Can one user operate multiple resources?
questions.answer: Not simultaneously - the RF logon binds the user to one resource at a time; switching requires logoff/logon to another resource.

questions.question: What does the RF 'skip' function do and its governance?
questions.answer: Skips the proposed task/WO to receive the next one; each skip can log a reason and excessive skipping is reported - unmanaged skipping undermines system-guided optimization.

questions.question: Where are RF verification profiles configured?
questions.answer: In RF framework customizing per logical transaction/step: which fields verify, against what, and whether entry or scan is required - tightening or relaxing floor discipline per process.

questions.question: What is the quick way to see which queue a stuck WO belongs to?
questions.answer: Monitor WO node with queue column, or the WO detail display - then cross-check that queue against resource group sequences to find who should be serving it.

questions.question: What is a handling unit (HU) in EWM?
questions.answer: A physical unit of packaging material plus contents (products or nested HUs) with a unique identifier - the object the warehouse physically moves, scans, stacks, and ships; EWM tracks stock inside HUs at bin level.

questions.question: What is a packaging material and its master data?
questions.answer: A product of packaging type (pallet, carton, tote) with dimensions, tare weight, and a packaging material type controlling HU behavior (number ranges, HU type derivation) - every HU references one.

questions.question: How do HU identifications get assigned?
questions.answer: From number ranges per packaging material type, or externally (SSCC-18 for shipping HUs); SSCC generation needs GS1 company prefix config - duplicate/exhausted ranges are rare but severe incidents.

questions.question: What is HU nesting?
questions.answer: HUs inside HUs (cartons on a pallet): EWM tracks hierarchies with content aggregation; moves of the top HU carry children - unpack/repack operations restructure hierarchies at work centers.

questions.question: Explain HU type vs packaging material type.
questions.answer: HU type classifies the physical unit class for logistics decisions (bin fit, conveyability); packaging material type governs technical behavior (numbering, defaults). HU type typically derives from the packaging material.

questions.question: What does 'HU-managed storage type' imply operationally?
questions.answer: All stock there exists inside HUs: every move is HU-based or creates/uses HUs; loose quantities need repacking at boundaries - accuracy and traceability up, ad-hoc handling flexibility down.

questions.question: What is a pick-HU?
questions.answer: The HU created for picking into (tote/carton) per WOCR packing profiles; it travels through packing/staging and may become the shipping HU or get repacked - the link between pick execution and shipment packaging.

questions.question: What happens to an HU at goods issue?
questions.answer: Its stock issues and the HU is deleted/closed in EWM (configurable), with data flowing to the ERP delivery (packing information/SSCC) for ASN and carrier messaging.

questions.question: What are common empty-HU pollution causes and cures?
questions.answer: Aborted flows leaving created-but-unused HUs, label reprints spawning shells, cancelled processes not cleaning up - cures: cleanup jobs for empty aged HUs, print-on-demand discipline, and process-complete checks (our duplicate-label incident).

questions.question: How do you repack stock between HUs systemically?
questions.answer: At packing work centers (/SCWM/PACK): move products/HUs between HUs with validation, printing new labels as needed - all movements logged; ad-hoc bin-side repacking is possible via RF but governed.

questions.question: What is the work center packing UI capable of?
questions.answer: Repacking, creating/closing HUs, weighing integration, deconsolidation, printing, exception handling, and difference reporting - configurable per work center layout to expose only needed actions.

questions.question: Why does HU weight/volume tracking matter downstream?
questions.answer: Carrier charges, load planning, and check-weigher validations rely on HU gross data (tare + contents); packspec/tare inaccuracies produce carrier disputes and weigher rejects - master data quality shows up at the scale.

questions.question: What is a shipping HU vs warehouse-internal HU?
questions.answer: Shipping HUs represent the units leaving to customers (SSCC-labeled, ASN-communicated); internal HUs organize warehouse handling (pick totes, decon pallets) and dissolve before shipping - one physical object can transition roles via repacking.

questions.question: How does check-weighing integrate?
questions.answer: Configured tolerance checks compare measured vs calculated HU weight at stations/automation; deviations route to clarification (repack/recount) - catching pick errors before the customer does.

questions.question: What is 'HU stock' vs 'bin stock' in queries?
questions.answer: Stock is always in bins, optionally structured in HUs at those bins; monitor queries can view either dimension - support must know both views to reconcile 'bin empty but HU shows stock' confusions (usually HU at different bin).

questions.question: What HU statuses matter for support?
questions.answer: Planned (created, not physical yet), in process, blocked, at work center, loaded - status filters explain why an HU refuses certain operations; blocked HUs after exceptions need explicit release paths.

questions.question: Can an HU exist without stock?
questions.answer: Yes - empty HUs (fresh created, or emptied by picks) exist as objects; they can be reused, moved, or deleted - unmanaged empties distort capacity checks (destination bins 'occupied' by shells).

questions.question: How are HUs handled in physical inventory?
questions.answer: HU-level counting: verify HU presence at bin (HU PI) vs content counting inside HUs - HU-managed areas often count via HU verification first (fast) with content sampling, reducing count effort dramatically.

questions.question: What printing accompanies HU lifecycle events?
questions.answer: Creation: HU label (with barcode/SSCC). Packing completion: content lists. Shipping: carrier labels per label determination. Reprints via PPF repeat - each with printer determination per station context.

questions.question: Explain 'HU as WT object' vs 'product WT into HU'.
questions.answer: HU WTs move the whole unit (source bin to destination); product WTs pick quantities INTO a (pick-)HU - both update HU/bin stock consistently; mixing up the two when analyzing task lists misleads root-causing.

questions.question: What is the impact of deleting an HU wrongly?
questions.answer: Contents become loose stock (or errors if HU-managed type), labels in circulation point at nothing, downstream documents referencing it break - deletion is guarded; investigation-first is the support rule.

questions.question: How do HUs map to ERP delivery packing data?
questions.answer: EWM packs deliver HU hierarchies into the ERP delivery's packing (HU) segment at GI/confirmation, feeding ASN and billing where packaging is billable - mapping issues surface as ASN/EDI rejections by customers.

questions.question: What are typical HU-related e-commerce design choices?
questions.answer: Pick-to-shipping-carton (cartonization pre-pick, no repack), SSCC at pick-HU creation, integrated carrier labeling at pack-out, and check-weigher gates - minimizing touches per parcel at high volumes.

questions.question: What is packaging specification's role for HU creation proposals?
questions.answer: Packspecs define target quantities per HU level enabling auto-palletization at GR and pick-HU sizing outbound; missing/wrong packspec equals manual packing decisions and inconsistent HU builds.

questions.question: A customer complains cartons arrive half-empty - system-side factors to review?
questions.answer: Cartonization/packing profile logic (cube utilization settings), packspec dimensions accuracy, WOCR item-to-HU distribution, product master cube data, and whether packers override proposals (measure override rate) - then fix data/logic before blaming labor.

questions.question: Can HU numbers be reused after deletion?
questions.answer: Number ranges normally do not recycle within their span; reuse risk comes from external numbering or range resets - both governed to avoid duplicate-identity incidents.

questions.question: What is a 'planned HU'?
questions.answer: An HU created system-side before physical existence (from palletization proposals) - it becomes real at confirmation; stale planned HUs from aborted flows need cleanup.

questions.question: How is tare weight handled in HU totals?
questions.answer: Gross = tare (packaging material master) + contents; wrong tare data corrupts check-weighing and carrier charges - a master data audit item.

questions.question: Which transaction is the HU monitor?
questions.answer: /SCWM/HUMO - search by HU, bin, product, or status with follow-on actions (repack, block, print); the first stop for any HU ticket.

questions.question: Can HUs hold mixed batches of the same product?
questions.answer: Yes if mixed-batch settings allow; batch-pure HU policies are common in pharma/food - enforced via packing validation and putaway mixed-storage rules.

questions.question: What is the PPF architecture in EWM?
questions.answer: Applications define actions (print, message, method calls) in action profiles attached to document objects; schedule and start conditions decide creation and execution timing; processing logs record outcomes - configured via SPPFCADM (PPF customizing) plus the EWM print condition record transactions, and monitored via SPPFP.

questions.question: What are schedule conditions vs start conditions?
questions.answer: Schedule condition: whether the action is generated at all for the document. Start condition: whether/when a generated action executes (immediately, at save, batch). Misunderstanding the pair is the top PPF-confusion in support.

questions.question: How does printing determination work for warehouse documents?
questions.answer: Condition technique: determination procedures with condition tables map context (warehouse, activity area, queue, work center, document data) to printer, form, and spool settings - maintained as condition records, evaluated at action execution.

questions.question: Which form technologies serve EWM outputs?
questions.answer: SmartForms and Adobe Forms for classic documents; label printing typically via SmartForms-to-label-printer languages or external label management (e.g., barcode label systems) integrated at spool/interface level.

questions.question: How do you analyze a 'label did not print' ticket end-to-end?
questions.answer: SPPFP: did the action exist and run (schedule/start)? Processing log: determination outcome (printer/form found?). SP01: spool created? Device (SPAD) reachable? Then physical printer/network - walk the chain in order and half the mystery disappears (printer incidents 6 and 25).

questions.question: What is action merging/deduplication in PPF?
questions.answer: Settings preventing duplicate actions for repeated document saves (process only once, replace older) - without them, documents re-saving spam duplicate outputs; with wrong settings, needed reprints never generate.

questions.question: How are failed PPF actions reprocessed at scale?
questions.answer: SPPFP mass selection by application/action/status with repeat processing after fixing the root cause; scheduled sweep jobs catch strays - a standing support routine with alerting on failure counts.

questions.question: What triggers exist for HU label printing?
questions.answer: HU creation (planned or at packing), putaway WT creation for pre-printing, work center actions, and manual reprint requests - design chooses trigger points balancing label availability vs reprint waste.

questions.question: What is delayed/batch execution of actions good for?
questions.answer: Decoupling heavy outputs (mass documents at wave release) from dialog response times: actions queue and process in background jobs - protecting floor UI latency at volume peaks.

questions.question: How does printer determination differ for RF-driven events?
questions.answer: Context comes from the resource/station rather than a fixed work center - condition tables include queue/resource criteria so a picker's confirmations print at the printer near them; stale mappings after floor moves misroute output (incident 25 pattern).

questions.question: What is the spool retention/troubleshooting basics for EWM support?
questions.answer: SP01 by user/device/date: check spool creation, output status, device errors; TemSe health and spool number range exhaustion are basis-side but EWM support recognizes their symptoms (nothing prints anywhere).

questions.question: What governance belongs around output condition records?
questions.answer: Change control with documentation (who mapped which station), periodic reconciliation against SPAD device inventory, and migration checklists for print-server changes - preventing our stale-device incident class.

questions.question: Can PPF call custom logic?
questions.answer: Yes - method actions execute ABAP classes (custom messages, interface pushes, validations); with power comes support surface: custom action failures need the same log discipline as standard ones.

questions.question: How do you test output changes safely?
questions.answer: QA with device simulation/print-to-spool-only, condition record scenarios per station context, then production pilot on one station before fleet rollout - output tests must include the physical last meter.

questions.question: What is an output 'storm' and its handling?
questions.answer: Mass reprocessing/document waves generating thousands of outputs flooding printers/spool; handling: throttled batch execution, spool quota awareness, and targeted reprocessing filters - plus stakeholder comms while queues drain.

questions.question: Which EWM documents typically carry printed output?
questions.answer: HU labels, pick lists/WO documents, delivery notes, loading lists, PI count documents, VAS instructions, and carrier shipping labels - each with its own determination context and failure modes.

questions.question: Where do you configure which action profile a document uses?
questions.answer: PPF customizing per application/document type assignment (e.g., HU application, delivery processing) - profiles bundle available actions; document context selects the profile at runtime.

questions.question: What is the interplay of PPF with alerts/workflow?
questions.answer: Actions can raise alerts or start workflows (exception notifications to leads); using PPF as the event-to-notification bridge standardizes operational alerting without custom event handling.

questions.question: Diagnose: everything prints twice at one station.
questions.answer: Duplicate condition records both matching (different tables in the access sequence), action merging disabled with double saves, or two active actions in the profile - the determination analysis + action log identifies which; fix data, not by unplugging the printer.

questions.question: Interview classic: pick list must print automatically when the wave releases - solution sketch?
questions.answer: WO document action with schedule condition on WO creation (from wave release), start condition immediate/batch per volume, printer determination by activity area/queue, forms per document type - plus failure alerting into the support queue; validate with a wave in QA.

questions.question: Where do you see why a PPF action was NOT created?
questions.answer: Check schedule condition evaluation - the determination analysis in PPF customizing test mode or application log shows condition results; a never-created action leaves no SPPFP entry, which itself is the clue.

questions.question: What is the difference between reprocessing and repeating an action?
questions.answer: Reprocessing retries a FAILED action; repeat generates a new execution of a successful one (reprints) - different buttons, different audit meaning.

questions.question: Can PPF actions run in parallel?
questions.answer: Batch-processed actions parallelize via job design; document-level sequential dependencies (label before list) need profile sequencing - race conditions here cause intermittent 'wrong order' printing mysteries.

questions.question: Name the spool transaction and two things you check there.
questions.answer: SP01: spool request existence/status and the output device error text - separating 'never spooled' from 'spooled but device failed'.

questions.question: How do you route output of one station temporarily to another printer?
questions.answer: Adjust the condition record (or device forwarding in SPAD for hard failures) with a documented rollback - ad-hoc SPAD forwarding without documentation creates the next incident.

questions.question: What log does a method-action write to?
questions.answer: The PPF processing log per action plus any application log (SLG1) the custom class writes - custom actions without logging are support nightmares; demand logging in code reviews.

questions.question: What is a typical cause of labels printing with stale data?
questions.answer: Action executed against an old document state (early trigger point) or form reading buffered data - re-trigger points and form data sourcing fix it, not reprint rituals.

questions.question: How do carrier label requirements enter EWM?
questions.answer: Via carrier-specific forms/label layouts selected by determination (carrier attribute) or external label systems called at pack-out - certification requirements per carrier drive the design.

questions.question: What monitoring do you set on PPF?
questions.answer: Scheduled failure-count alerts per application/action type with thresholds, plus a daily sweep report - silent PPF failure accumulation is among the most common chronic EWM debts.

questions.question: Interview one-liner: why is PPF preferable to custom event coding?
questions.answer: Standardized triggering, logging, reprocessing, and determination - you inherit an operations model instead of building one; custom events need all four rebuilt.

questions.question: Which PI procedures does EWM support?
questions.answer: Periodic (annual wall-to-wall), continuous (spread over the year, bin-triggered), cycle counting (product-class frequency driven), and ad-hoc counts (event-triggered: denials, damage); plus low-stock/zero-stock checks during operations.

questions.question: What is the PI area concept?
questions.answer: PI is organized by activity areas designated for counting: documents target bins per PI area assignment - structuring count waves geographically/organizationally.

questions.question: Explain cycle counting configuration.
questions.answer: Products classify (A/B/C/D via indicators, often slotting/value-driven) with per-class count frequencies; the system proposes due bins/products per schedule - focusing effort where value/velocity is.

questions.question: What is a low-stock check?
questions.answer: Opportunistic verification when bin quantity drops below a threshold at picking: the picker confirms the remaining count cheaply during normal work - accuracy maintenance nearly free of dedicated labor.

questions.question: What is zero-stock check?
questions.answer: When a pick should empty a bin, the picker confirms it is indeed empty - catching hidden quantities immediately at the cheapest possible moment; discrepancies trigger investigation/adjustment flows.

questions.question: Walk through the PI document lifecycle.
questions.answer: Create (per procedure/scope) > activate/print or send to RF > count entry (RF or work center) > recount decisions if deviating > difference determination > difference posting to the difference analyzer > ERP posting of accepted differences - with authorizations and tolerances gating each stage.

questions.question: How does RF counting work ergonomically?
questions.answer: System-guided bin sequence per activity area sorting, scan bin > scan/enter contents (HUs, products, quantities), blind or informed counting per config - blind counts are more accurate, slower; design picks per area criticality.

questions.question: What are counting tolerances and tolerance groups?
questions.answer: Value/percentage thresholds per user group: differences within tolerance post automatically; beyond it, recounts or higher-authorization approval are enforced (our incident 7) - balancing control with throughput.

questions.question: What is the difference analyzer's role?
questions.answer: The clearing cockpit for count differences: analyze, recount-request, accept/post to ERP (adjusting both systems), or investigate - with document trail; differences must not rot there, aging KPIs apply.

questions.question: When do PI differences post to ERP and what happens there?
questions.answer: Upon acceptance in the difference analyzer: goods movements adjust ERP stock (with accounting impact), synchronized with EWM bin adjustments - finance-relevant, hence tolerance and approval design matters.

questions.question: How is PI reconciled with ongoing operations?
questions.answer: Bins under active count get blocked for movements (or counted in quiet windows); design minimizes operational freeze via cycle/continuous methods instead of wall-to-wall shutdowns - modern EWM PI is a background process, not an event.

questions.question: What is HU-level PI?
questions.answer: Counting confirms HU presence/identity at bins without opening (label scan), with content counts sampled or triggered by suspicion - massively faster in full-HU reserve areas; content accuracy rides on receiving/packing discipline.

questions.question: Legal/audit requirements around annual inventory - how does EWM satisfy them?
questions.answer: Documented complete coverage via procedures (periodic or continuous covering all bins yearly, cycle counting where jurisdiction accepts), signed difference postings, and audit-trail reports of counts/adjustments - compliance is procedure + evidence, not one big count day per se.

questions.question: What triggers ad-hoc PI sensibly?
questions.answer: Pick denials/zero-stock surprises, damage events, clarification-zone processing, negative stock detection, and post-incident verification (our relabeling case) - codified via exception-code follow-ons creating count tasks automatically.

questions.question: How do you keep PI progress visible during a large count?
questions.answer: Monitor PI nodes: documents by status, counted vs open bins per area, difference value accumulation - progress dashboards per hour during wall-to-wall events with recount backlog tracking.

questions.question: Common causes of stock accuracy erosion between counts?
questions.answer: Unconfirmed/aged WTs, exception shortcuts (denials without investigation), uncontrolled manual bin entries, HU repacking without system updates, and interface stock divergence - accuracy is process discipline, PI only measures it.

questions.question: What is the relation between PI and the ERP inventory?
questions.answer: EWM owns bin-level PI entirely; ERP receives only difference postings (sloc-level adjustments) - ERP-side PI transactions are not used for EWM-managed locations; auditors sometimes need this explained.

questions.question: Recount policy - how to design it well?
questions.answer: Automatic recount above thresholds by different counter, second recount by supervisor for high values, acceptance authority mapped to tolerance groups - documented, so counts do not become negotiations.

questions.question: How would you run PI for bulk lanes with stacked pallets?
questions.answer: Count by lane/HU-count verification with contour assumptions (full-lane counts via HU multiplication), sample-open stacks per policy, and accept measured-quantity procedures for weight-based goods - method fits physics, not clipboard idealism.

questions.question: Stock accuracy KPI design - what do you recommend?
questions.answer: Bin-level accuracy (bins clean/counted), quantity accuracy by value, denial rate trend, difference value per period vs threshold, aging of unresolved differences, and count coverage vs plan - reported monthly with root-cause Pareto on differences.

questions.question: Which transaction creates PI documents?
questions.answer: /SCWM/PI_CREATE (and procedure-specific creation via the PI cockpit /SCWM/PI_PROCESS); RF executes counts; the difference analyzer (/SCWM/DIFF_ANALYZER) settles outcomes.

questions.question: What is an 'informed' vs 'blind' count?
questions.answer: Informed shows expected quantities to the counter (fast, bias-prone); blind hides them (accurate, slower) - choose per area value/risk profile.

questions.question: Can you count during active picking in the same bin?
questions.answer: The bin is blocked for the count's duration; scheduling counts against quiet windows per area avoids operational conflict - continuous PI design minimizes the overlap.

questions.question: Who may accept differences above tolerance?
questions.answer: Users whose tolerance group covers the value, typically supervisors/inventory controllers - with authorization objects gating the difference analyzer actions (incident 7's lesson).

questions.question: What happens to a PI document nobody completes?
questions.answer: It ages: bins stay blocked or fall out of compliance coverage - aged-PI-document monitoring belongs in the weekly sweep with escalation to inventory control.

questions.question: How do you evidence 100% yearly coverage for auditors?
questions.answer: Coverage reports of counted bins/products vs totals with dates, plus procedure documentation - generated from PI history, archived with sign-offs.

questions.question: What triggers a recount automatically?
questions.answer: Difference beyond configured thresholds - the document flows back to counting (ideally a different counter) before difference processing; recount policy is configuration plus SOP.

questions.question: Does EWM PI post to FI directly?
questions.answer: No - EWM posts stock differences to ERP inventory management, which drives the FI postings per standard account determination; EWM support ends at the material document, finance owns valuation questions.

questions.question: What is a count 'per storage bin' vs 'per product'?
questions.answer: Bin-based counts everything in selected bins (layout-driven); product-based targets a product across bins (suspicion-driven) - both supported, chosen per trigger.

questions.question: Rapid design answer: 99.9% bin accuracy target - main levers?
questions.answer: Zero/low-stock checks active, denial-triggered ad-hoc counts, cycle counting weighted to A-movers, HU discipline at receiving/packing, and relentless investigation closure - PI procedures are the measurement, execution discipline is the lever.

questions.question: Name the replenishment types in EWM.
questions.answer: Planned replenishment (scheduled min/max-based), order-related (triggered by open pick demand shortfall), automatic (triggered at bin threshold crossing during confirmations), and direct replenishment (in-process during a denial with immediate task) - plus crate-part/exception variants per release.

questions.question: How does planned replenishment calculate quantities?
questions.answer: For fixed bins below minimum: refill toward maximum, rounded per packspec units (whole cases/pallets), sourced from reserve per removal strategy - executed by a scheduled job filtered by warehouse/type/area.

questions.question: What is the trigger logic of automatic replenishment?
questions.answer: At WT confirmation reducing pick-face stock below minimum, the system immediately generates a replenishment WT - no job latency; suits high-velocity faces where waiting for the nightly run means denials.

questions.question: Order-related replenishment pros/cons?
questions.answer: Pro: replenishes exactly what open demand needs (minimal face inventory, no dead stock). Con: adds latency inside the pick window and races picking - requiring queue prioritization and lead-time buffering (Day 9 linkage).

questions.question: Which master data drives replenishment?
questions.answer: Fixed bin assignments with min/max, product replenishment settings (type, quantities), packspec rounding units, and the removal strategy for the source side - min/max quality decides everything (Day 3 linkage).

questions.question: How do you prioritize replenishment vs picking work?
questions.answer: Dedicated replenishment queues with priority above picking for critical faces, resource dedication in peak windows, and monitoring face-stock health (below-min report) as a leading indicator instead of waiting for denials.

questions.question: What is slotting's optimization logic in EWM?
questions.answer: Rule-based calculation combining demand data (frequency/quantity), physical data (dimensions/weight), and requirement profiles into recommended storage parameters: storage type/section, bin type, fixed bin, and max quantities - simulated, then activated to the product master.

questions.question: What inputs must be clean before trusting slotting?
questions.answer: Cube/weight accuracy, representative demand history or forecast, correct packspecs, and sensible condition/requirement settings - slotting amplifies data quality in both directions (Day 3's garbage-in warning).

questions.question: What is the difference between slotting activation and rearrangement?
questions.answer: Activation writes recommended parameters to the product master (affecting future putaway); rearrangement creates tasks to physically move existing stock to match the new placement - parameter change vs stock migration.

questions.question: How do you run rearrangement without disrupting operations?
questions.answer: Scoped runs (area/product class) in low-activity windows, capacity-limited task batches, priority below operational work, and progress monitoring - a rolling optimization, not a big-bang move weekend (usually).

questions.question: When should slotting run?
questions.answer: Periodically (quarterly/seasonally), at assortment changes (new products, promotions), and after demand-pattern shifts - with simulation review before activation; continuous slotting without governance creates churn.

questions.question: What KPI evidence shows slotting/replenishment working?
questions.answer: Falling denial rate, shorter pick paths (travel per pick), stable face-stock health (rare below-min alarms), fewer emergency replenishments, and improved picks-per-hour - measured before/after activation waves.

questions.question: What is a 'requirement/condition profile' in slotting terms?
questions.answer: Configuration describing how demand and product properties translate into storage requirements (e.g., velocity thresholds to section preferences) - the tunable business logic of the optimizer.

questions.question: Two-bin vs min/max replenishment thinking in EWM?
questions.answer: Classic two-bin (refill when one empties) approximates via min set to one bin's content; EWM's min/max with packspec rounding generalizes it - interviewers like hearing you map floor practices to config.

questions.question: Exception scenario: replenishment creates tasks but faces stay empty - causes?
questions.answer: Tasks routed to unserved queues, priority starvation under pick load, source stock locked/absent (reserve empty - a procurement/planning issue surfacing in the warehouse), or physical non-execution (tasks open, aging report catches it) - each with a different owner.

questions.question: What is 'exception-based' (direct) replenishment at denial?
questions.answer: The denial exception immediately generates replenishment from reserve and optionally re-queues the pick - self-healing flow turning an error into recovery without supervisor touch; configuration per exception code chain.

questions.question: Kanban/production-supply replenishment vs warehouse replenishment?
questions.answer: Production supply (PSA staging) follows production demand semantics (crate parts, release quantities) with its own machinery; keep concepts separated in answers - EWM covers both but with different configuration paths.

questions.question: How does seasonality get handled in fixed-bin strategy?
questions.answer: Seasonal slotting runs re-classifying velocity, temporary face expansions (secondary fixed bins), and pre-season rearrangement waves - plus discipline in de-slotting after season to reclaim prime locations.

questions.question: What monitoring belongs in a replenishment health dashboard?
questions.answer: Faces below minimum (count/aging), open replenishment WTs vs takt, denial rate by area, emergency replenishment share, and source-side stockouts - reviewed each shift in high-velocity operations.

questions.question: Design case: 500 fast SKUs, denials spike every morning 8-10 - solution reasoning?
questions.answer: Diagnosis: overnight demand consumed faces and the planned run undersizes refills or runs too early. Fixes: raise max toward daily-demand coverage where capacity allows, add an automatic-replenishment threshold for the top movers, resequence the planned job closer to shift start, and prioritize replenishment queues in that window - verified via before/after denial trend.

questions.question: Which job runs planned replenishment and its key filters?
questions.answer: The replenishment planning run (/SCWM/REPL background variant) filtered by warehouse, storage types/areas, and products - variant hygiene is the incident-8 lesson (hardcoded areas rot).

questions.question: Can replenishment cross warehouses?
questions.answer: No - replenishment works within one warehouse number; cross-warehouse restocking is a stock transfer/transport process at ERP level.

questions.question: What prevents replenishment tasks from flooding a congested aisle?
questions.answer: Queue capacity awareness via resource allocation, task bundling through WOCR, and staggering the planning run per area - plus physical-aware slotting keeping refill sources near faces.

questions.question: Is slotting available in basic (embedded) licensing?
questions.answer: Slotting and rearrangement are advanced-EWM licensed features - license scoping questions belong in design phases, not discovered at activation attempts.

questions.question: What is a quick health query for face stock?
questions.answer: Monitor stock node filtered on fixed-bin storage types with quantity below minimum - exportable as the below-min report feeding the shift dashboard.

questions.question: Should safety stock live in pick faces or reserve?
questions.answer: Reserve - faces sized for cycle demand plus replenishment lead time; hoarding safety stock in faces wastes prime slots and increases count effort; reserve absorbs variability.

questions.question: What data does rearrangement need before execution?
questions.answer: Released slotting results (new placements), move priority rules, and capacity windows - it generates product WTs; execution monitoring treats it like any internal movement wave.

questions.question: How do promotions get slotted temporarily?
questions.answer: Temporary fixed-bin assignments in promo zones with dated validity, order-related replenishment for the spike, and de-slotting tasks scheduled at promo end - a rehearsed playbook, not improvisation.

questions.question: One metric proving replenishment timing is wrong?
questions.answer: Denials clustering in specific hours (faces emptying between runs) - timing/quantity misfit visible in hour-of-day denial histograms.

questions.question: Rapid answer: difference between min/max and demand-driven quantities?
questions.answer: Min/max is static threshold logic; order-related calculates from live open demand - static suits stable movers, demand-driven suits volatile/slow items; mixed designs are normal.

title: Stock Types, Posting Changes & QM Integration

questions.question: What is a stock type in EWM?
questions.answer: The classification of stock usability: unrestricted (F), quality inspection (Q), blocked (B), returns/other types - each mapped with availability groups to ERP storage locations; process behavior (ATP, removal eligibility) hangs on it.

questions.question: How do availability groups and stock types map to ERP?
questions.answer: The combination stock type + availability group resolves to an ERP storage location: e.g., F+002 = AFS (sellable), F+001 = ROD (on dock), Q+002 = quality sloc - the translation layer keeping ERP location-accurate while EWM works bins (Day 1/5 linkage).

questions.question: What is a posting change and its flavors?
questions.answer: A stock attribute change without necessarily moving it: stock type transitions (Q to F at usage decision, F to B for damage), owner/party changes, batch reclassification - executed via posting change deliveries/WTs, synchronized to ERP as transfer postings.

questions.question: When does a posting change require physical movement?
questions.answer: When target stock types live in different physical areas by design (blocked stock cage) - the posting change couples with a transfer WT; otherwise it is book-only at the same bin ('posting change in the bin').

questions.question: Walk through QM-integrated receiving.
questions.answer: GR of inspection-relevant product creates stock type Q plus an inspection document/lot (via inspection rules mapping to ERP QM or decentralized inspection); quality inspects (sample at work center or full stock), records the usage decision, and the UD triggers posting change to F (accept) or B/return (reject) - stock flowing per the decision (incident 23 background).

questions.question: What are inspection rules in EWM?
questions.answer: Configuration defining which receipts are inspection-relevant (by product, vendor, process) and how: inspection object type, sample handling, counters/skip logic - the EWM-side contract with QM lot creation.

questions.question: What happens when the usage decision rejects stock?
questions.answer: Posting change to blocked/return stock type, routing to quarantine/returns areas via strategies filtered by stock type, vendor claim processes downstream - with full traceability from lot to final disposition.

questions.question: How do stock type transitions synchronize to ERP and what breaks?
questions.answer: Posting change messages post ERP transfer postings between slocs; breaks: mapping gaps (missing sloc for a combination - incident 9), queue failures leaving split realities (incident 4), and period/movement blocks ERP-side - monitor posting-change errors explicitly.

questions.question: What is 'stock in transfer' between availability groups used for outbound staging?
questions.answer: Designs mirroring dock readiness in ERP move staged stock to a GI-availability group so ATP stops seeing it and ERP knows dock inventory - adding accuracy at the cost of extra posting volume (Day 8 linkage).

questions.question: Scrapping from the warehouse - process sketch?
questions.answer: Post to blocked, physically consolidate at a scrap zone, approval workflow per value policy, then goods issue to scrap (cost center/order account assignment) synchronized to ERP with material document evidence - segregation of duties throughout.

questions.question: How are vendor returns processed stock-type-wise?
questions.answer: Blocked/return stock type at claim decision, outbound return delivery to vendor referencing the original receipt where possible, GI closing the loop - stock types keep claim inventory out of ATP throughout.

questions.question: What are 'special stocks' EWM handles?
questions.answer: Consignment (vendor-owned), sales order stock (E), project stock (Q per WBS) - separated logically by stock attributes/owner; processes must carry the special-stock reference through every movement (frequent custom-code breakage point).

questions.question: How does batch status interplay with stock types?
questions.answer: Batch restrictions (restricted/unrestricted batch status) overlay stock types: a restricted batch in F-stock still blocks usage per batch logic - two gates, both must open; support distinguishes which one closed.

questions.question: Explain a clean quality-hold ('stock freeze') for a suspect product warehouse-wide.
questions.answer: Product-level process block plus mass posting change of on-hand to Q/blocked, open-task handling (cancel/redirect picks), ERP alignment verification, then controlled release after investigation - a rehearsed recall-drill procedure, not improvisation.

questions.question: What reporting proves stock-type integrity to auditors?
questions.answer: Reconciliation reports per stock type/sloc between EWM and ERP (zero-difference evidence), posting-change audit trails with users/timestamps, and blocked-stock aging with disposition documentation - integrity is reconciliation plus traceability.

questions.question: Which stock type letters should you know cold?
questions.answer: F unrestricted, Q quality inspection, B blocked, plus returns and customs/special variants per configuration - the letters map to ERP stock categories through availability groups.

questions.question: Can stock change type without a posting change document?
questions.answer: No - stock type transitions always post (document trail); anything else would break ERP synchronization and auditability.

questions.question: Where do you monitor failed posting changes?
questions.answer: Monitor nodes for posting-change deliveries with error status plus the queue monitors carrying their ERP messages - part of the daily sweep.

questions.question: What is an availability group in one sentence?
questions.answer: A grouping key on EWM stock that, combined with stock type, maps to exactly one ERP storage location - EWM's location-translation mechanism.

questions.question: Sales order stock in the warehouse - the support catch?
questions.answer: Every movement must carry the sales order assignment (special stock E); mixing it with anonymous stock or losing the reference in custom flows creates ATP chaos - test custom code against special stocks always.

questions.question: Consignment stock ownership at GI?
questions.answer: Vendor-owned until withdrawal: GI/consumption triggers the ownership transfer posting - EWM tracks the owner throughout; settlements ride on that accuracy.

questions.question: Quick QM answer: what creates the inspection lot?
questions.answer: The GR of inspection-relevant stock per inspection rule triggers lot creation (ERP QM or EWM-side inspection document) - no rule match, no lot, stock sits in Q unresolved (incident 23).

questions.question: Batch status vs stock type - which wins?
questions.answer: Both gate independently: restricted batch in F-stock is still unusable; support must check both flags before declaring stock 'available'.

questions.question: What is a posting change 'in the bin'?
questions.answer: Book-only stock attribute change at the same physical bin (no move) - fast for status flips where physical segregation is not required by design.

questions.question: Where does scrapping value hit?
questions.answer: ERP material document from the scrap GI drives the P&L posting per account determination; EWM provides the executed movement and its evidence trail.

questions.question: What are the three commonest stock-type incident patterns?
questions.answer: Mapping gaps for new combinations (incident 9), queue-lost posting changes splitting realities (incident 4), and Q-stock without inspection documents after master-data gaps (incident 23) - the guide's trio.

questions.question: Blocked stock keeps appearing in ATP - first check?
questions.answer: Verify the stock actually carries blocked type in EWM AND the mapped sloc is ATP-excluded in ERP scope - misconfigured ERP ATP scope masquerades as an EWM bug.

questions.question: Who approves blocked-to-unrestricted releases?
questions.answer: Quality/inventory control per SOP with authorization-gated posting changes - never floor-level self-service; segregation of duties is audit-relevant.

questions.question: Special stock and PI - the catch?
questions.answer: Counts must respect special stock segments (count per owner/assignment); merging counts across owners corrupts settlements - PI scope design includes stock attributes, not just bins.

questions.question: One-line answer: why do availability groups exist at all?
questions.answer: So ERP keeps meaningful storage-location-level visibility (ATP, MRP, finance) while EWM owns physical bin truth - two granularities, one consistent translation.

questions.question: Why are exception codes central to a stable EWM operation?
questions.answer: They convert floor deviations into structured, automated system responses (follow-on actions, alerts, documents) with analytics - without them every deviation becomes an unstructured supervisor conversation and a data lie somewhere.

questions.question: What configuration makes up an exception code?
questions.answer: Code with business context (process/step where valid), internal exception classification, follow-on actions (task changes, stock investigation, alerts, workflow), and authorization requirements - assigned per execution step matrices (incident 17's missing-entry lesson).

questions.question: Give five exception codes every EWM warehouse needs.
questions.answer: Pick denial/bin empty, HU or product damaged, bin overflow at putaway, wrong/unreadable identification (label issues), and quantity difference at counting/receiving - each with tested follow-on chains.

questions.question: What is the warehouse monitor's architecture?
questions.answer: Hierarchical node trees (documents, stock, resources, processes) with filters, drill-downs, and follow-on function bindings - extensible with custom nodes; variants tailor views per role. It is both the support cockpit and a mass-action tool.

questions.question: Which monitor nodes do you check first each morning in AMS?
