questions.answer: Failed/aged queues (both systems), open WT aging, wave status vs cutoffs, PPF failures, posting-change errors, clarification-zone stock, below-min pick faces, and negative stock - a 15-minute health sweep with documented thresholds.

questions.question: What are alert types in the alert monitor worth configuring?
questions.answer: Overdue deliveries/waves, queue failures, resource inactivity, capacity overflow of staging areas, and interface stock-comparison differences - each routed (email/queue ticket) with severity mapping to the on-call procedure.

questions.question: How do you structure severity levels for EWM incidents?
questions.answer: S1: warehouse/dock stopped or stock integrity broken (GI failures, MFS down, queues dead). S2: process degraded with workaround (single station down, print failures with fallback). S3: individual document/data issues. S4: questions/cosmetics - with response/resolution SLAs and escalation paths per level.

questions.question: What belongs in an EWM support runbook?
questions.answer: Queue handling SOP (both systems, never-delete rule), monitor morning-sweep checklist, GI/GR failure triage trees, MFS restart procedure, wave-recovery steps, stock reconciliation procedure, print troubleshooting chain, escalation contacts, and change-freeze calendars - versioned and drilled.

questions.question: How do you handle 'business says X is missing but system shows confirmed'?
questions.answer: Trust neither by default: verify document trail (who confirmed, when, from which resource/station), physical check at the claimed and system locations, camera/HU trail where available - then correct the layer that lied (usually an exception shortcut on the floor).

questions.question: What is a stock investigation task/flow?
questions.answer: Exception-triggered verification work: count the suspect bin, trace last movements, decide correction (adjustment posting with reason) - closing the loop that a denial opened; unresolved investigations rot accuracy KPIs.

questions.question: What ticket categories dominate steady-state EWM AMS statistically?
questions.answer: Interface/queue issues, output/printing, determination failures (bin/packspec/staging), master data gaps for new products, exception-flow questions, and authorization issues - your knowledge base should have runbook articles matching this Pareto.

questions.question: What is proactive support vs reactive in EWM context?
questions.answer: Proactive: monitoring jobs catching failures before business notices (queue alerts, reconciliation runs, PPF sweeps), health KPIs trended weekly, and recurring-cause elimination (problem management). Reactive-only EWM support guarantees repeated severity-1 mornings.

questions.question: How do you safely use monitor mass actions during recovery?
questions.answer: Precise filters double-checked, tiny pilot batch first, physical-reality confirmation per batch, evidence logging (before/after exports), and four-eyes on destructive operations - recovery speed never justifies unverified mass postings (Day 10 linkage).

questions.question: What is your framework for root cause analysis write-ups?
questions.answer: Timeline (what happened when), technical cause chain (first failure to business impact), why-detection-failed analysis, corrective actions (immediate + preventive with owners/dates), and verification evidence - the incident guide's per-ticket structure is exactly this framework.

questions.question: Interview scenario: recurring Monday-morning queue failures - your systematic approach?
questions.answer: Pattern analysis (what runs weekends: jobs, maintenance, interface partners down), correlate failure timestamps with weekend events, identify the dependency (e.g., partner system restarts resetting sessions - the MFS incident pattern at interface scale), fix the dependency or add resilience (retry/reconnect logic, sequenced startup checks), and verify across following weekends with monitoring evidence.

questions.question: Your first three clicks on any 'delivery stuck' ticket?
questions.answer: Document flow in /SCWM/PRDI-PRDO (status/blocks), queue check both systems for its messages, application log around its timestamps - orientation before hypotheses.

questions.question: What is a monitor variant and why standardize them?
questions.answer: Saved node/filter layouts per role; standardized variants make the morning sweep reproducible across the team and shift handovers lossless.

questions.question: Name three healthy operational thresholds worth alerting on.
questions.answer: Queue entries older than 5 minutes, open WTs older than shift-length, PPF failures above single digits per hour - tuned per site, but the pattern is age/count thresholds on flow objects.

questions.question: What is a hypercare period and its staffing logic?
questions.answer: Post-go-live intensive support (on-site floor presence, war-room, daily defect triage) until KPIs stabilize - staffed with build-team knowledge before handing to steady-state AMS with runbooks.

questions.question: How do you keep a knowledge base actually used?
questions.answer: Runbook articles indexed by symptom (not by module), linked from ticket categories, updated as a closure requirement for novel incidents - the incident guide's format is the article template.

questions.question: What belongs in shift handover for warehouse support?
questions.answer: Open severities with next actions/owners, degraded components and workarounds active, planned changes/jobs due, and watch items (thresholds trending badly) - written, not verbal-only.

questions.question: When do you escalate to SAP (OSS/case)?
questions.answer: Reproducible standard-behavior defects after note search, with a minimal reproduction, system/support data ready - parallel to (not instead of) local workaround engineering.

questions.question: How do you find relevant SAP Notes efficiently?
questions.answer: Search by message class/number and component (SCM-EWM-*) with release filters; note search skill is a real support productivity differentiator.

questions.question: What is a problem record vs incident in EWM AMS?
questions.answer: Incidents restore service; problems eliminate recurring causes (the Pareto's top items) with root-cause projects - mature accounts fund problem management explicitly.

questions.question: Change freeze policy around peak - your recommendation?
questions.answer: Freeze non-emergency transports through peak windows with an emergency board for exceptions - most self-inflicted severities are transports landing at the wrong time (multiple incidents in the guide).

questions.question: What evidence closes a severity-1 credibly?
questions.answer: Restoration proof (KPIs back, business confirmation), cause statement, and dated preventive actions - closure without prevention is a scheduled recurrence.

questions.question: Which SLG1 objects are EWM-relevant?
questions.answer: Delivery processing, PPF, MFS, and interface logs under /SCWM/* and /SCDL/* application log objects - date/user-filtered SLG1 reading is a daily support skill.

questions.question: What is your stance on production debugging?
questions.answer: Read-only analysis freely; variable-changing debug in production only under emergency change control with four-eyes - one wrong F8 posts wrong stock (authorization design should enforce this).

questions.question: Monitoring vs observability for EWM - interview angle?
questions.answer: Monitoring alerts known failure modes (queues, jobs); observability means being able to answer new questions from logs/traces without new instrumentation - runbook maturity plus log discipline gives EWM teams practical observability.

questions.question: Rapid close: three habits of low-severity EWM sites?
questions.answer: Relentless queue/PPF hygiene automation, transport discipline with data-dependency checklists, and exception-code coverage so floor deviations self-document - boring operations are engineered, not lucky.

questions.question: What does EWM yard management cover?
questions.answer: Checkpoint check-in/out of transportation units, yard bins (parking, doors) with TU moves between them, door assignment, and visibility of trailer inventory - the truck-side mirror of bin management.

questions.question: What is a transportation unit vs vehicle?
questions.answer: The vehicle is the tractor/truck entity; the TU is the cargo-carrying unit (trailer/container) that docks, holds deliveries, and is loaded/sealed - one vehicle may bring multiple TUs.

questions.question: How does check-in flow work at the gate?
questions.answer: Register arrival at the checkpoint (TU/carrier data), assign to parking or door per determination/dispatcher, yard move tasks track physical repositioning, and status updates flow to dock planning (incident 22's determination dependencies).

questions.question: What is dock appointment scheduling relative to yard management?
questions.answer: DAS plans carrier time slots in advance (capacity-leveled dock calendar); yard management executes the arrival reality - integrated, they close the plan-vs-actual loop at the dock.

questions.question: What are seals and their process role?
questions.answer: Seal numbers captured at loading completion/departure verify cargo integrity; mismatches at receiving trigger security/claims flows - simple data field, heavy compliance weight in some industries.

questions.question: Define transportation cross-docking vs merchandise distribution.
questions.answer: Transportation CD: inbound HUs flow directly to outbound doors for onward transport (hub operations) without storage. Merchandise/retail distribution: pre-allocated push flows to stores. Opportunistic CD: system matches open outbound demand with arriving stock ad hoc (Day 8 linkage).

questions.question: What must be true for opportunistic cross-docking to fire?
questions.answer: Activation in configuration, timing windows aligning (demand open when stock arrives), stock/demand compatibility (product, quantity, stock type), and process types allowing redirection - otherwise stock quietly does normal putaway and nobody notices the missed savings.

questions.question: What is a VAS order?
questions.answer: The work document for value-added services (labelling, repacking, kitting steps, quality activities) executed at work centers with materials consumption tracking, linked to inbound/outbound documents - the auxiliary work companion to deliveries.

questions.question: How do packspecs relate to VAS?
questions.answer: VAS-relevant packspec levels/work steps describe the service content (which labels, which added materials), driving VAS order generation and station instructions - master data again steering execution.

questions.question: Kitting: kit-to-order vs kit-to-stock in EWM.
questions.answer: Kit-to-order: kits assemble against specific outbound demand (components picked to kitting, finished kit ships - incident 21's hierarchy dependency). Kit-to-stock: kits pre-built via VAS/production-like orders into inventory as new SKU - different documents, same physical station often.

questions.question: What is reverse kitting?
questions.answer: Disassembling kits back into components (returned kits, obsolete bundles) via VAS orders reversing the BOM consumption - inventory accuracy for both kit and components maintained through the order.

questions.question: How does labor tracking work at VAS/kitting stations?
questions.answer: Work center confirmations capture who/what/how long per VAS order; with Labor Management active, engineered standards compare planned vs actual for these indirect activities too (Day 20 linkage).

questions.question: What master data does a kitting operation need?
questions.answer: Kit header product, kit BOM/packspec structure with component quantities, VAS-relevant settings, station work centers with layouts, and printer determination for kit labels - plus ERP-side alignment so orders explode correctly.

questions.question: Common yard-management support tickets?
questions.answer: TUs stuck in wrong status blocking door assignment, check-in failures from determination gaps (incident 22), yard stock (trailer inventory) mismatches after manual moves, and DAS slot conflicts - mostly master data and status-flow issues.

questions.question: Design question: retailer wants store-friendly pallets (aisle-sequenced) - which capabilities combine?
questions.answer: Store-layout-sequenced picking (sort sequence per store profile), pick-to-pallet with WOCR consolidation by store/aisle group, VAS for price labelling, and load sequencing by drop order - EWM assembles it from sorting, WOCR, VAS, and staging/loading configuration.

questions.question: Which transaction handles check-in/check-out?
questions.answer: /SCWM/CICO at checkpoints, with yard moves via /SCWM/YMOVE and TU processing in the shipping cockpit environment.

questions.question: Can a TU carry mixed deliveries for multiple doors?
questions.answer: Yes - multi-stop/multi-door plans assign the TU sequentially; door determination and loading sequences must then be TU-plan aware.

questions.question: What master data do doors need for cold chain?
questions.answer: Door master data with the determination-group mappings (staging area/door groups) covering temperature-class requirements - the exact gap in incident 22.

questions.question: What is a yard bin technically?
questions.answer: A storage bin in a yard-role storage type - parking spots and door positions addressable like bins so TUs are 'stock' the monitor can find.

questions.question: Trailer inventory - why do sites lose track of it?
questions.answer: Manual yard moves without system updates; the fix is disciplined RF yard moves and periodic yard checks (yard PI analog) - trailers are bins on wheels.

questions.question: What triggers VAS order creation?
questions.answer: Delivery items with VAS relevance (packspec work steps/auction determination) at document creation - no relevance data, no VAS order, station waits for nothing (kit incident analog).

questions.question: Are VAS consumables inventory-managed?
questions.answer: Yes if modeled: labels/dunnage as components consumed per VAS order posting - or expensed bulk if immaterial; design decides the accuracy/effort trade.

questions.question: Kit header stock - when does it exist?
questions.answer: Kit-to-stock creates header-SKU inventory; kit-to-order never stocks the header (components ship as the kit) - ATP and PI treat the two totally differently.

questions.question: What breaks kits most often at the interface?
questions.answer: Missing item hierarchy links (higher-level item references) flattening the structure - incident 21's exact pattern; contract tests on hierarchy fields prevent it.

questions.question: Opportunistic cross-docking measurement?
questions.answer: Share of eligible demand actually cross-docked plus touches-saved estimate; if near zero, timing windows or activation scope are wrong - a savings feature nobody notices failing.

questions.question: Who assigns doors when determination fails?
questions.answer: Dispatcher via manual TU-door assignment with authorization - monitored as an exception rate; chronic manual assignment means determination data rot.

questions.question: What is a loading sequence and who defines it?
questions.answer: Drop-order-driven HU load order (last stop loaded first); route/stop data defines it, loading tasks enforce it via scan sequence - wrong sequences surface as customer-site unloading complaints.

questions.question: Seal capture failure at departure - severity?
questions.answer: Compliance-relevant for regulated freight (blocked departure until captured) - configuration decides enforcement; support must know which flows hard-block versus warn.

questions.question: Can yard management work without DAS?
questions.answer: Yes - check-in/door/yard moves stand alone; DAS adds the planning calendar layer; many sites run yard-only first, DAS later.

questions.question: Rapid design: 40 doors, 200 trucks/day, congestion chaos - first three system levers?
questions.answer: DAS slots leveling arrivals, determination-driven door assignment by route/temperature/dock capability, and yard-move discipline with live TU visibility - then measure dwell time per stage to iterate.

questions.question: What is EWM Labor Management (LM)?
questions.answer: Planned-vs-actual labor performance measurement: engineered labor standards calculate target times per activity; actual confirmations measure performance, feeding utilization views, incentives, and planning - activated per warehouse/activity scope.

questions.question: What are engineered labor standards (ELS)?
questions.answer: Formulas computing expected duration per work unit from parameters (distance, quantity, weight, HU counts) - maintained as formulas/services in LM configuration; credibility with the workforce depends on their fairness and maintenance.

questions.question: What is a work unit in LM?
questions.answer: The measured chunk of work (a WO's execution, a VAS order) that gets planned duration, actual duration, and an executing resource - the atom of labor analytics.

questions.question: How does LM handle indirect labor?
questions.answer: Indirect activities (cleaning, meetings, downtime) record via indirect labor tasks so utilization math distinguishes performance from availability - without it, performance metrics unfairly punish assigned-but-idle time.

questions.question: What organizational sensitivities accompany LM rollouts?
questions.answer: Works councils/unions typically must approve individual performance measurement; anonymized/aggregated reporting modes and transparent standard-setting processes are the successful pattern - technical activation is the easy part.

questions.question: What planning value does LM add beyond measurement?
questions.answer: Workload preview (planned hours from open/forecast work vs available staff) enables shift-level capacity decisions - moving staffing from gut feel to calculated demand curves.

questions.question: What is MFS in one paragraph?
questions.answer: The Material Flow System is EWM's built-in warehouse control layer talking directly to PLCs of automation (conveyors, ASRS, sorters) via telegrams over communication channels - eliminating a separate WCS for supported topologies: EWM decides AND executes routing at machine level.

questions.question: Explain the MFS object model.
questions.answer: Communication points (decision/reporting locations on the automation), communication channels (PLC connections), telegram definitions (message structures), and resources (automation equipment like cranes) - mapped onto LOSC routing so tasks execute leg by leg via telegrams.

questions.question: What is a telegram lifecycle?
questions.answer: EWM sends a move order telegram to the PLC, PLC acknowledges, executes, reports arrival at the next communication point; EWM confirms the leg and issues the next - sequence numbers and life-sign telegrams guard the session (incident 18's reset lesson).

questions.question: What happens when a telegram fails validation?
questions.answer: Error handling per channel/telegram type: park for clarification, alert, or automatic responses - clarification queues for unknown HUs at scanners (no-read handling to a clarification lane) keep the line moving while support investigates.

questions.question: What is a 'no-read' and its standard handling?
questions.answer: Scanner cannot identify an HU: automation routes it to a clarification/exception lane per default decision, EWM flags it for manual identification and re-induction - no-read rate is a core automation health KPI (label quality proxy).

questions.question: How do you monitor MFS health?
questions.answer: The MFS nodes of the warehouse monitor (/SCWM/MON): communication channel status, telegram backlogs and retry entries, ack timing, and MFS resource states; plus alerting on frozen ack counters and queue growth - with the automation vendor's PLC view side by side in the control room.

questions.question: What is the coordination model between EWM support and automation vendors?
questions.answer: Joint runbooks (restart sequences - who restarts what in which order), shared incident bridges for line-down events, clear demarcation (telegram log as the objective interface evidence), and change coordination for PLC/EWM software updates - the interface is contractual, not just technical.

questions.question: Capacity/flow control in MFS - what exists?
questions.answer: Communication point capacity settings, buffer-zone management, and release throttling prevent overloading segments; upstream, wave sizing respects automation takt (Day 9 linkage) - flow control failures show as physical accumulation and timeout cascades.

questions.question: Interview scenario: crane throughput dropped 30% with no errors anywhere - approach?
questions.answer: Compare telegram timing statistics historically (ack-to-completion per move), segment the drop (one crane/aisle or all), check double-cycle ratio (interleaving degradation from task-mix changes), review recent wave/WOCR changes altering task patterns, and inspect PLC-side mechanical logs with the vendor - data first, then joint diagnosis; no-error slowdowns are usually pattern changes, not faults.

questions.question: Is LM part of basic or advanced EWM?
questions.answer: Advanced licensing - like MFS, slotting, and yard/DAS; scoping answers belong in every design interview.

questions.question: What activates LM measurement for an activity?
questions.answer: LM activation per warehouse plus external process steps flagged relevant, with formulas/services assigned - activation without maintained standards produces meaningless targets.

questions.question: Where do actual times come from?
questions.answer: Task/WO confirmation timestamps per resource (RF events) - no manual timekeeping; data quality equals confirmation discipline.

questions.question: What is a 'performance document'?
questions.answer: The LM record aggregating an employee's work units per period for evaluation/incentive interfaces - the auditable unit HR-side integrations consume.

questions.question: Name two classic ELS formula parameters.
questions.answer: Travel distance (from bin coordinates) and quantity/weight handled - plus HU counts and fixed time constants per activity step.

questions.question: What is MFS's alternative for complex automation sites?
questions.answer: A vendor WCS layer between EWM and PLCs (EWM sends tasks, WCS handles machine control) - chosen when automation topology exceeds MFS scope or vendor mandates it; interface design then shifts to the WCS boundary.

questions.question: What is a communication point capacity check?
questions.answer: Limits on HUs allowed at/behind a point preventing physical overload - EWM holds telegrams until space frees; misconfigured capacities cause artificial starvation or real jams.

questions.question: Life-sign telegram - purpose?
questions.answer: Periodic heartbeat proving the PLC session alive; missing life-signs trigger channel error handling - the first thing frozen-ack incidents (18) violate.

questions.question: Can MFS run in embedded S/4 EWM?
questions.answer: Yes - MFS is available in embedded advanced EWM; the automation layer does not require decentralized deployment.

questions.question: What is a double cycle for a crane?
questions.answer: Combining a putaway and retrieval in one movement cycle (in on the way, out on the return) - the interleaving concept at machine level; its ratio is a throughput KPI.

questions.question: Telegram trace - where?
questions.answer: MFS monitor telegram logs per channel with payload history - the objective evidence in EWM-vendor demarcation discussions; retention settings matter for incident forensics.

questions.question: What staffing does an automated site's support need?
questions.answer: 24x7 or on-call coverage matching production hours, MFS-trained responders with the restart runbook, and a vendor escalation contract with response SLAs - automation downtime is measured in money per minute.

questions.question: Emergency operation when automation dies?
questions.answer: Degraded-mode SOPs: manual paths around automated segments where physically possible (LOSC alternate routing), throttled waves, and prioritized recovery sequence - designed and drilled in advance, not invented during the outage.

questions.question: How do LM results feed staffing plans?
questions.answer: Planned hours from open/forecast workload (via standards) vs roster availability highlight gaps per shift/area - the workload preview turning LM from measurement into planning.

questions.question: Rapid close: three metrics for an automation cockpit?
questions.answer: Telegram ack latency trend, no-read rate, and segment throughput vs takt - with queue backlogs as the early-warning overlay.

title: S/4HANA Embedded EWM, Migration, Debugging & Career

questions.question: What are the key differences working in embedded EWM vs decentralized 9.x?
questions.answer: No CIF for most master data (direct core access), synchronized delivery documents without cross-system qRFC, Fiori app landscape, simplified stock reconciliation, and one transport landscape - support loses whole error classes but must learn S/4-specific integration internals.

questions.question: What is the migration path from classic WM to EWM?
questions.answer: Assessment (process fit, basic vs advanced), greenfield redesign or migration tooling for master data (bins, fixed bins, stock), process re-mapping (WM movement types to EWM process types conceptually), integration switch of the sloc to EWM-managed, cutover with stock upload validation - WM decommissioning ends the compatibility clock.

questions.question: What migration tools support WM-to-EWM moves?
questions.answer: The EWM migration cockpit for warehouse data (bins, products, stock), standard load programs/BAPIs, and template-based mass maintenance - plus custom validation reports comparing WM vs EWM state at cutover; SAP Readiness Check informs the timing.

questions.question: What is a typical EWM cutover weekend skeleton?
questions.answer: Freeze + final counts, WM/legacy stock extract, load bins/fixed bins/products (pre-loaded weeks before), stock upload with HU construction, delivery cutover (drain WM, redirect new to EWM), interface switches, validation counts (system vs physical sampling), go/no-go gate, hypercare rota start - all rehearsed twice in dress runs.

questions.question: How do you debug determination issues efficiently in EWM?
questions.answer: Prefer built-in analysis first: WT simulation logs, packspec determination analysis, PPF processing logs, wave logs - then targeted /h debugging at the determination function modules with reproducible cases in QA; blind full-trace debugging is the amateur pattern.

questions.question: Which BAdIs do EWM consultants meet most?
questions.answer: Determination influence points (process type, storage type search, WOCR filtering/sorting), exception follow-on customization, delivery interface enrichment, RF flow modifications, and MFS telegram processing hooks - always documented with a business-rule registry so support knows custom logic exists.

questions.question: What is the CDS/analytics angle in embedded EWM?
questions.answer: Standard CDS views expose warehouse data for Fiori analytical apps and embedded analytics (workload, stock, performance) - replacing many custom monitor extensions and BW extracts for operational reporting.

questions.question: How do transports/change management differ for EWM vs ERP-only teams?
questions.answer: Same transport machinery, but EWM changes often pair customizing with master data dependencies (bins, condition records) that transports do NOT carry - cutover checklists per change (the recurring incident theme: config transported, data forgotten).

questions.question: What testing strategy fits EWM changes?
questions.answer: Layered: determination simulations for config, scenario end-to-end scripts per process family (Day 5/7 matrices), RF device testing physically, volume tests for waves/automation, and regression packs for the incident-prone areas (queues, PPF, GI) - automated where APIs allow, evidence-based always.

questions.question: What differentiates a senior EWM support consultant in interviews?
questions.answer: They narrate diagnosis paths (log to root cause chains), know the data/config/execution layer separations, cite prevention patterns not just fixes, quantify with KPIs, and demonstrate interface fluency (qRFC/PPF/MFS internals) - the incident guide's structure is exactly the storytelling template.

questions.question: A hiring manager asks: your first 30 days on our EWM AMS account - plan?
questions.answer: Week 1: runbooks, monitoring inventory, open-ticket Pareto, shadow the morning sweep. Week 2: master data and config walkthrough of the top processes, meet floor supervisors. Week 3: own S3/S2 tickets with mentor review, document knowledge gaps. Week 4: propose the top-3 recurring-cause eliminations with evidence - value delivered inside the first month, not just onboarding consumed.

questions.question: Explain a complete EWM outbound failure story you would tell in an interview (structure).
questions.answer: Context (business impact, urgency), first observation (monitor/queue evidence), hypothesis tree walked (what you excluded and why), root cause with proof, fix with verification, prevention shipped - 3 minutes, KPI-quantified; prepare three such stories: one interface, one determination, one automation/output.

questions.question: What certifications/learning paths exist for EWM?
questions.answer: SAP certification for Extended Warehouse Management (S/4HANA-based editions), SAP Learning Hub journeys, and hands-on CAL/trial systems - but interviewers weight demonstrable troubleshooting stories and config depth far above certificates alone.

questions.question: Where is EWM heading (relevant for interview vision questions)?
questions.answer: Deeper S/4 embedding with Fiori-first operations, warehouse robotics integration standards maturing, cloud deployment options expanding, and analytics/AI-assisted optimization (slotting, labor forecasting) - core config skills stay, the surface modernizes.

questions.question: Final drill: list the 10 transactions you would defend as your daily EWM toolkit.
questions.answer: /SCWM/MON (monitor), /SCWM/PRDI and /SCWM/PRDO (delivery processing), /SCWM/RFUI (RF), SMQ1/SMQ2 (queues), SPPFP (PPF), /SCWM/PACK (work center), /SCWM/LS03 plus the monitor's bin node for mass changes (bins), /SCWM/BINMAT (fixed bins), /SCWM/ERP_STOCKCHECK (reconciliation), and SM37 with SLG1 (jobs and logs) - each mapped to the incident classes it solves.

questions.question: What replaced /SCWM/ transaction habits in Fiori-first shops?
questions.answer: Fiori apps for warehouse tasks, deliveries, and monitoring (Warehouse Monitor app included) - transactions persist, but new-user onboarding increasingly starts Fiori-side; consultants need both vocabularies.

questions.question: Is there still a CIF queue to monitor in embedded EWM?
questions.answer: Largely no for master data; delivery/goods-movement synchronization still has internal queues/logs to watch - fewer failure classes, not zero monitoring.

questions.question: What is the Stock Room Management trap in migrations?
questions.answer: Treating it as a destination: it is compatibility scope with restricted features - a bridge with an end date in planning terms, and interviewers probe whether you know its limitations.

questions.question: Name three cutover validation reports you would build.
questions.answer: Bin count/attribute comparison (legacy vs EWM), stock quantity/value reconciliation per product/sloc with HU counts, and open-document drain verification (zero legacy open TOs/deliveries at switch) - each with signed evidence.

questions.question: First debugging step for custom code suspicion?
questions.answer: Check the business-rule registry/BAdI implementation list for the process, then set targeted breakpoints at the documented enhancement spots - spelunking without the registry wastes hours (and argues for keeping one).

questions.question: How do you test RF changes without devices?
questions.answer: RF runs in SAP GUI (/SCWM/RFUI desktop mode) for logic testing; device-specific rendering/scanner behavior still needs physical spot checks - both stages, always.

questions.question: What ATC/code-quality gates fit EWM custom development?
questions.answer: Standard ATC variants plus EWM-specific reviews: special-stock handling, lock behavior in RF flows, queue-safe interface coding, and log/error-handling presence - the recurring custom-code failure themes.

questions.question: One migration risk unique to HU-managed conversions?
questions.answer: Constructing accurate HU hierarchies from legacy data (often HU-less) - stock uploads must invent HUs matching physical reality, or day-one counts diverge instantly; physical HU labeling during preparation is the underestimated workstream.

questions.question: What does 'clean core' mean for EWM extensions?
questions.answer: Prefer released BAdIs/APIs over modifications, keep enhancements documented and isolated, and use side-by-side extensibility where volumes/UX justify - upgrade cost control as an architectural principle.

questions.question: How would you prepare for an EWM support interview in 21 days using this series?
questions.answer: Days 1-7 foundations and inbound, 8-14 outbound/execution internals, 15-21 specialties and operations - daily: 30 Q&A active recall, one incident narrated aloud from the companion guide, and one monitor/transaction walked in a practice system; interviews reward narrated diagnosis fluency over memorized definitions.

questions.question: What distinguishes S/4 embedded EWM stock visibility for support?
questions.answer: Single database: MMBE-family and EWM stock views reconcile within one system, and inconsistencies shrink to synchronization states rather than cross-system drift - reconciliation becomes verification, not archaeology.

questions.question: Your closing pitch as an EWM AMS candidate in two sentences?
questions.answer: I run warehouses boring: queues clean, monitors quiet, and recurring causes eliminated with evidence. When they are not boring, I diagnose in structured layers - data, configuration, execution, interface - and I document every fix so the team gets faster, not just the ticket closed.

questions.question: Which three incident stories from the companion guide map to the most-asked interview themes?
questions.answer: The qRFC SYSFAIL chain (integration depth), the GI stock-determination mismatch (stock model mastery), and the wave release timeout (batch/volume operations) - rehearse them in the Description-Analysis-RootCause-Resolution rhythm.

questions.question: What is the single most underrated EWM support skill?
questions.answer: Reading logs in the right order (document flow, then queue, then application log, then trace) before forming hypotheses - discipline that halves resolution times and is completely trainable.

questions.question: Final question: why hire a support-focused EWM consultant over a pure build consultant?
questions.answer: Support consultants know how designs fail under volume, time pressure, and human deviation - they build the missing 20% (monitoring, exceptions, runbooks) that turns a go-live into a stable operation; the best projects staff both perspectives.
